summary: Generates barcodes for stock locations from barcode rules, with the base typed in by a user or taken from a sequence. Open a location form, set a rule, and use the Generate Barcode button. Needs the abstract barcode generator module, and the rule setup is described there.

name: barcodes_generator_location
summary: Generates barcodes for stock locations from barcode rules, with the base typed in by a user or taken from a sequence. Open a location form, set a rule, and use the Generate Barcode button. Needs the abstract barcode generator module, and the rule setup is described there.

name: barcodes_generator_package
summary: Generates barcodes for product packagings, such as cases or boxes, from barcode rules. The base is typed in or taken from a sequence. Use the Generate Barcode button on the product packaging form.

name: barcodes_generator_product
summary: Generates EAN13 barcodes for products and variants from a barcode rule pattern, with the base typed in by a user or taken from a sequence. Use the Generate Barcode button on the product form. Users need to be in the Generate Barcodes group to manage rules on products.

name: barcodes_generator_product
summary: Generates EAN13 barcodes for products and variants from a barcode rule pattern, with the base typed in by a user or taken from a sequence. Use the Generate Barcode button on the product form. Users need to be in the Generate Barcodes group to manage rules on products.

name: base_archive_security
summary: Adds a Can archive records group, which controls who may archive or unarchive records. All users have it by default, and you can restrict archiving to some users by removing the group from the others.

name: base_bank_from_iban
summary: Fills in the bank automatically when an IBAN bank account is entered on a contact, by matching the bank code in the IBAN with a bank record. Set the bank code on each bank under Contacts > Configuration > Bank Accounts > Banks, and the bank is selected for you when there is a match.

name: base_bank_from_iban
summary: Fills in the bank automatically when an IBAN bank account is entered on a contact, by matching the bank code in the IBAN with a bank record. Set the bank code on each bank under Contacts > Configuration > Bank Accounts > Banks, and the bank is selected for you when there is a match.

name: base_binary_url_import
summary: Wizard for bulk-importing files such as PDFs or text documents from URLs into a chosen file field on many records at once. Records are listed by database ID or XML ID, and the wizard is found under Settings > Technical. Size and timeout limits can be changed through system parameters.

name: base_business_document_import
summary: Technical base shared by the supplier invoice import and the sales order import modules. It adds no screens of its own, and provides the common methods those modules use to read business documents.

name: base_business_document_import
summary: Technical base shared by the supplier invoice import and the sales order import modules. It adds no screens of its own, and provides the common methods those modules use to read business documents.

name: base_business_document_import_iban
summary: Validates IBAN bank accounts found while importing business documents, when IBAN validation is installed. A glue module that adds no screens of its own.

name: base_business_document_import_phone
summary: Lets imported invoices and sales orders find the right contact by phone or mobile number. When phone validation is installed, numbers are stored in E.164 format, which makes matching reliable. A glue module that adds no screens of its own.

name: base_business_document_import_phone
summary: Lets imported invoices and sales orders find the right contact by phone or mobile number. When phone validation is installed, numbers are stored in E.164 format, which makes matching reliable. A glue module that adds no screens of its own.

name: base_cancel_confirm
summary: Technical base that gives document models a confirmation dialog when Cancel is clicked, asking for a reason that is then shown on the form. Provides no feature on its own; other modules use it for their cancel buttons.

name: base_cancel_confirm
summary: A base feature that adds a confirmation popup asking for a reason when a document's cancel button is clicked, and shows that reason on the form. It does nothing on its own and is switched on for specific apps such as sales or purchases through system parameters. Developers use it to add the same behavior to other documents.

name: base_changeset
summary: Holds changes to chosen fields for approval. Instead of saving a direct edit, the change is queued as a changeset, which an approver accepts or rejects, and only accepted values are written to the record. Rules define which fields need validation, and the list is under Configuration > Record Changesets > Changesets.

name: base_comment_template
summary: Provides reusable comment templates, written with Mako, that print above or below the lines of a document such as an order or invoice. Templates are chosen by model, company, partner and a domain, with a priority. Created under Settings > Technical > Reporting > Comment Templates, and other comment template modules build on it.

name: base_comment_template
summary: Technical base for predefined comment text printed on business documents such as quotations, invoices and delivery orders. Templates can be set per company, per partner and per model, filtered by a domain, and placed above or below the document lines. They are managed under Reporting comment templates in developer mode, and other modules build on this one.

name: base_company_legal_info
summary: Adds Legal Name and Legal Type fields to the company, such as Ltd, SARL or GmbH, and shows them on the report layout used for official documents like quotations and invoices. The name field stays as the trade name. Set them on the company form.

name: base_conditional_image
summary: Lets any model show images chosen by conditions on the record's fields and company, and stores each image once so it can be changed in one place. The images are configured under Technical Settings > Settings > Images. Cannot be used together with base_multi_image.

name: base_conditional_image
summary: Lets admins define images that change depending on record details, such as a different logo per company or a default image for records that match a condition. The same image is stored once and reused, so changing it updates every matching record. Images are set under Settings, Technical, Images.

name: base_country_state_translatable
summary: Makes country state names translatable, so states can be shown in the user's language. This is a base module for localization modules, which add the translations for each country. It has no screens of its own.

name: base_cron_exclusion
summary: Lets admins mark scheduled actions that must not run at the same time, so two heavy jobs never overlap. The setting is on the scheduled action form under a Mutually Exclusive Scheduled Actions tab. It is a technical setting found under Settings, Technical, Automation, Scheduled Actions.

name: base_cron_exclusion
summary: Lets you choose scheduled actions that must not run at the same time as the one you are editing, so they cannot overlap. Set it under Settings > Technical > Automation > Scheduled Actions, in the Mutually Exclusive Scheduled Actions tab.

name: base_currency_iso_4217
summary: Adds the ISO 4217 numeric code and full name to currencies, and updates existing currencies in Odoo to match the standard. The fields appear on the currency record.

name: base_currency_iso_4217
summary: Adds the ISO 4217 numeric code and full name to currencies, and updates existing currencies in Odoo to match the standard. The fields appear on the currency record.

name: base_custom_filter
summary: Lets admins add their own search filters, group-by options and search fields to list views, shown in the standard filter and group-by menus. They are created under Settings, Custom Filters, and can be limited to chosen user groups. It helps teams find records faster on each app's screen.

name: base_custom_filter
summary: Lets administrators define custom searches, filters and group-by options for a model's search bar, configured under Settings > Custom Filters. The filters then appear in that model's Filters and Group By menus for the users allowed to see them.

name: base_delivery_carrier_label
summary: Technical base for shipping label generation. Adds a Send to shipper button on transfers, carrier options that can differ by transfer, and a manifest wizard. Packages are grouped into one for shipping by default, which carrier connectors need, and carrier-specific modules plug in on top of it.

name: base_delivery_carrier_label
summary: Technical base for shipping label generation. Adds a Send to shipper button on transfers, carrier options that can differ by transfer, and a manifest wizard. Packages are grouped into one for shipping by default, which carrier connectors need, and carrier-specific modules plug in on top of it.

name: base_dns_infrastructure
summary: Stores DNS domain zones and their DNS records in Odoo, with owners, renewal dates and record types that validate their values. It is used to keep a manual record of DNS entries. Provider connectors are separate modules.

name: base_dns_infrastructure
summary: Stores DNS domain zones and their DNS records in Odoo, with owners, renewal dates and record types that validate their values. It is used to keep a manual record of DNS entries. Provider connectors are separate modules.

name: base_domain_inverse_function
summary: Technical helper that splits a normalized search domain back into its parts, the inverse of combining conditions with AND and OR. Developers use it when they need to add conditions to an existing domain. Nothing for end users.

name: base_ebill_payment_contract
summary: Technical base that attaches an eBill payment contract to each customer, with a service, start and end dates, and a validity flag. Alone it does nothing. It needs an e-billing connector module installed, which supplies the actual transmission method.

name: base_ebill_payment_contract
summary: Technical base that attaches an eBill payment contract to each customer, with a service, start and end dates, and a validity flag. Alone it does nothing. It needs an e-billing connector module installed, which supplies the actual transmission method.

name: base_edi
summary: Technical base that groups EDI features. It adds an EDI home menu item, a general EDI security group and an EDI module category. Nothing here for end users on its own.

name: base_edi
summary: Technical base that groups EDI features. It adds an EDI home menu item, a general EDI security group and an EDI module category. Nothing here for end users on its own.

name: base_edifact
summary: Technical library that generates and parses UN/EDIFACT D96A messages, used by EDI modules such as the EDIFACT sales order import. It stores partner GLN identifiers, which need the GLN identification module. Nothing to use on its own.

name: base_exception
summary: Technical base for customizable exception rules, which flag problems on documents such as sales orders and invoices and can block them until resolved or ignored. It is not useful alone; other modules such as sale_exception and purchase_exception apply it to their documents.

name: base_exception
summary: A base framework for defining configurable exception rules, such as blocking a sale order when a condition is not met. It provides the exception popup and resolution wizard that other modules use. It is not useful alone; it shows up in the apps that build on it, like sales or purchase exceptions.

name: base_export_anonymize
summary: Anonymizes chosen fields in exports for users in a special group, including exports reached through related fields. Mark the fields under Settings > Technical > Database Structure > Fields Export Anonymize, and change the placeholder text through system parameters.

name: base_export_async
summary: Adds an Asynchronous export checkbox to the export screen. The export runs in a background job, and the resulting CSV or XLS file is emailed to the user who started it. Useful for large exports.

name: base_export_manager
summary: Lets administrators manage saved export templates, which Odoo stores but does not show, and adds an Export Access right per model so exporting can be allowed or blocked for each group. Create templates from the Export wizard in any list view, and set the access right in the Access Rights tab of a group.

name: base_export_manager
summary: Lets admins manage the export templates that users save, and adds an export access right per model so some groups can be blocked from exporting data. Export templates are kept under Settings, Technical, User Interface, Export Templates. It is useful for controlling data leaving the system.

name: base_external_dbsource
summary: Lets administrators define connections to other databases, using ODBC, Firebird, Oracle client or SQLAlchemy, for use by other modules. Connections are set up under Database Sources in the technical settings and store the connection string and password. It is a technical integration base.

name: base_external_dbsource
summary: Defines connections to external databases through ODBC, Firebird, Oracle Client or SQLAlchemy, so other modules can read data from them. Created under Settings > Technical > Database Structure > Database Sources, with a name, connector, connection string and password.

name: base_external_dbsource_mssql
summary: Adds Microsoft SQL Server as a connector for external database sources, using SQLAlchemy. Set it up as a database source under Settings > Technical > Database Structure > Database Sources, with the connection string and password.

name: base_external_dbsource_mssql
summary: Adds SQL Server (MSSQL) support to external database sources, connecting through SQLAlchemy. It is set up in the same place as the base database sources. It is a technical connector.

name: base_external_dbsource_mysql
summary: Technical add-on that lets Odoo read data from an external MySQL database. Once installed, a MySQL option is available when you create a database source under Settings > Technical > Database Structure > Database Sources, so you can enter the connection string and password.

name: base_external_dbsource_mysql
summary: Adds MySQL support to external database sources, connecting through SQLAlchemy. It is set up under Database Sources in the technical settings. It is a technical connector.

name: base_external_dbsource_sqlite
summary: Adds SQLite file support to external database sources, connecting through SQLAlchemy. It is set up under Database Sources in the technical settings. It is a technical connector.

name: base_external_dbsource_sqlite
summary: Technical add-on that lets Odoo read data from an external SQLite database file. It adds SQLite as a connector choice when you create a database source under Settings > Technical > Database Structure > Database Sources.

name: base_external_system
summary: Technical base module that keeps a single list of remote systems (host, port, username, password, private key, remote path) that other modules can connect to. These records are managed under Settings > Technical > External Systems, and the credentials are stored as plain text, so a security add-on is recommended.

name: base_external_system
summary: A technical base for storing connection details to remote systems, with fields for host, port, username, password and private key, plus a common client interface that other modules use. Credentials are stored in plain text, so encryption has to come from another module. Systems are configured under External Systems in the technical settings.

name: base_external_system_odoorpc
summary: Technical add-on that lets an External System record point at another Odoo instance using JSON-RPC, so code can read records from a remote Odoo. It adds a Test Connection button on the record under Settings > Technical > External Systems and is mainly used for migrations and syncs from older Odoo versions.

name: base_facturx
summary: Technical base module for Factur-X and ZUGFeRD electronic invoices, which embed structured XML inside a PDF invoice. It does nothing on its own; it is required by the invoice and invoice import Factur-X modules, and it needs UNECE codes set on units of measure, taxes and payment methods.

name: base_facturx
summary: Technical base module for Factur-X and ZUGFeRD electronic invoices, which embed structured XML inside a PDF invoice. It does nothing on its own; it is required by the invoice and invoice import Factur-X modules, and it needs UNECE codes set on units of measure, taxes and payment methods.

name: base_fontawesome
summary: Technical web add-on that adds Font Awesome 6.7.2 icons to Odoo, so any free Font Awesome icon can be used in views and widgets. Icons can be set as solid, regular or brand styles, and the module version matches the icon library version.

name: base_fontawesome
summary: Technical web add-on that adds Font Awesome 6.5.1 icons to Odoo, so any free Font Awesome icon can be used in views and widgets. Icons can be set as solid, regular or brand styles, and the module version matches the icon library version.

name: base_fontawesome
summary: Adds the Font Awesome 6.5.1 icon library to Odoo so icons can be used in views, websites and reports. Solid, regular and brand icon styles are supported. It is a technical resource with no new screens for users.

name: base_fontawesome_web_editor
summary: Makes Font Awesome 6.7.2 and newer icons display correctly in the website and web editor. It installs automatically once the web editor and base Font Awesome modules are present. Users see the icons in the editor without any extra setup.

name: base_force_record_noupdate
summary: Technical tool that adds a Force No-Update checkbox on a model's definition, so records of that model are protected from being overwritten when a module is upgraded. It is found on the model form under Settings > Technical > Database Structure > Models, and it is hidden from the regular app menus.

name: base_force_record_noupdate
summary: Lets admins mark a model so its data is protected from being overwritten when modules are upgraded. The option is a checkbox on the model form under Settings, Technical, Models, labelled Force No-Update. It is a technical safeguard for developers and administrators.

name: base_geoengine
summary: Technical GIS add-on that brings maps and spatial queries into Odoo, backed by PostGIS and OpenLayers. Administrators define raster and vector map layers and add spatial columns to models, which then appear as map views, and it requires a PostGIS-enabled database.

name: base_geoengine
summary: Technical GIS add-on that brings maps and spatial queries into Odoo, backed by PostGIS and OpenLayers. Administrators define raster and vector map layers and add spatial columns to models, which then appear as map views, and it requires a PostGIS-enabled database.

name: base_geoengine_demo
summary: Demo add-on that shows the geospatial features with a sample ZIP area model and a retailing machine model that have map fields. It is for testing and learning how map views work, not for production data, and it is built on base_geoengine.

name: base_geoengine_demo
summary: Demo add-on that shows the geospatial features with a sample ZIP area model and a retailing machine model that have map fields. It is for testing and learning how map views work, not for production data, and it is built on base_geoengine.

name: base_geolocalize_company
summary: Adds latitude, longitude and a geolocation date to each company record, which is useful when you run several companies and want to place them on a map. A Company Assignation tab on the company form lets you type coordinates or use the Geolocate button to fill them in automatically.

name: base_global_discount
summary: A base module that defines global discounts, which can apply to sales or purchases, and lets customers and suppliers carry their own discount lists. On its own it adds little. The accounting or purchase global discount module is what makes it show on documents. Discounts are managed under Global Discounts in settings.

name: base_global_discount
summary: Base module for global discounts that apply to sales or purchases, such as a standard discount for a group of customers. It creates the discount rules under Settings > Parameters > Global Discounts and assigns them on the Sales & Purchases tab of a partner, but it does nothing alone until account_global_discount or purchase_global_discount is installed.

name: base_google_map
summary: Adds Google Maps support to Odoo, including map views and widgets such as address autocomplete and a marker icon picker. Administrators enter the Google Maps API key, theme, language and region under Settings > General Settings > Google Maps View, and the module installs base_geolocalize.

name: base_group_backend
summary: Technical security module that adds two Backend User groups, giving some users access to the Odoo back office with fewer permissions than the standard Internal User group. Users in the UI group get only their own data and a minimal menu (notifications and activities), and they are assigned on the user form under Access Rights.

name: base_group_backend
summary: Adds two restricted Backend User groups that give access to the backend only, without the full Internal User permissions, so custom modules cannot quietly widen access. One of the groups also gives the user interface and a minimal menu. Use it for controlled back-office users.

name: base_group_subcontractor
summary: Adds a restricted user type called Subcontractors that gives backend access with only the minimum permissions, exposing just the Discuss menu. Any further permissions must be granted through customisation. Use it for outside contractors who only need to chat.

name: base_ical
summary: Publishes read-only calendar feeds (ICS links) built from chosen Odoo records, such as events, that users can subscribe to in calendar apps. Each feed is set up with a model and an optional domain, and users enable it on their profile. Use it to show Odoo data in Nextcloud or other calendars.

name: base_import_async
summary: Adds a checkbox on the CSV import screen that runs the import as a background job, so large files do not tie up the screen. Big files are split into chunks, and any failure shows in the job status, which is tracked through the queue_job framework.

name: base_import_async
summary: Lets users run large CSV imports in the background so the screen does not hang while the file loads. A checkbox on the import screen queues the import, which is split into chunks, and any failure shows up as an error on the background job. Users can open the job queue to read the error.

name: base_import_default_enable_tracking
summary: Small technical tweak that switches on the Track history during import option by default when you import records. The checkbox only shows in debug mode, so the chatter history of imported records gets logged without extra clicks.

name: base_import_match
summary: Lets imports detect existing records by fields other than the XML ID, such as VAT, email or name, so imported rows update the right record instead of creating duplicates. Match rules are set under Import Match in the technical settings. Use it when syncing data from other systems.

name: base_import_match
summary: Lets you set rules that decide whether a CSV import should update an existing record or create a new one, based on fields such as name, VAT or email instead of only the external ID. Rules are set under Settings > Technical > Database Structure > Import Match, and by default companies are matched on VAT.

name: base_import_odoo
summary: Copies records from another Odoo database into this one, for merging databases, one-way syncs, or pulling together data from several systems. You set it up under Settings > Remote Odoo import > Import configurations, choose the models and optional domain filters, and a cron job runs the import and shows its progress on the form.

name: base_import_pdf_by_template
summary: Imports PDF files and creates records from the text in them, such as turning a supplier document into a record in any model. You define a template with patterns that say where each value sits, under Settings > Technical > Base Import PDF Simple > Templates, and then use the Import records (with template) action.

name: base_import_pdf_by_template_account
summary: Connects PDF templates to invoicing, so a PDF attached to an email sent to an invoice alias is turned into a vendor or customer invoice. It also adds an Invoice Templates menu under Invoicing > Configuration > Management for accounting managers.

name: base_import_security_group
summary: Makes CSV and Excel import a permission. Only users with the Import CSV/Excel files box ticked on the Access Rights tab of their user form see the Import records button under Favorites, and the backend blocks batch imports for everyone else.

name: base_import_security_group
summary: Makes importing CSV and Excel files a permission that admins can grant per user, using an Import CSV/Excel Files checkbox on the user form. Users without it no longer see the Import records button in list and kanban views, and batch imports are blocked on the server too. It is used to keep data loading restricted.

name: base_import_security_group
summary: Makes CSV and Excel import a permission. Only users with the Import CSV/Excel files box ticked on the Access Rights tab of their user form see the Import records button under Favorites, and the backend blocks batch imports for everyone else.

name: base_iso3166
summary: Technical data module that adds the standard ISO 3166 country codes to each country record: 3-letter alpha-3 codes, numeric codes and formerly used codes. It mainly serves other modules that need these codes, and it adds the Country Code (3-letter) and Country Code (numeric) fields on countries.

name: base_iso3166
summary: Technical data module that adds the standard ISO 3166 country codes to each country record: 3-letter alpha-3 codes, numeric codes and formerly used codes. It mainly serves other modules that need these codes, and it adds the Country Code (3-letter) and Country Code (numeric) fields on countries.

name: base_kanban_stage
summary: Technical base module that adds stages for kanban boards, so records can be moved between columns such as New, In Progress and Done. Other developers can add stage-based kanban to their own models, and administrators manage the stages under Settings > Technical > Kanban > Stages.

name: base_kanban_stage
summary: Technical base module that gives other models a stage, priority, color and assignee so their records can be shown as cards in Kanban columns. End users do not use it directly, but apps that adopt it get stage-based Kanban boards and the stage setup screens. Stages are stored as Kanban Stage records tied to a model.

name: base_location
summary: Lets you fill in a partner's city, state, country and zip automatically by entering a zip code. It uses zip records linked to cities, which you create under Contacts > Configuration > Localization. It also adds better search filters for locations.

name: base_location
summary: Lets you fill in a partner's address by typing the zip code. Once the zip is set, the city, state and country fill in automatically. Zips and cities are maintained under Contacts, Configuration, Localization.

name: base_location_geonames_import
summary: Imports cities and zip codes from the Geonames database for chosen countries. It is found under Contacts > Configuration > Localization > Import from Geonames. For each selected country, entries not found in the new download are removed before the import.

name: base_location_geonames_import
summary: Adds a wizard that loads cities and zip codes for the countries you pick from the Geonames database. It is found under Contacts, Configuration, Localization, Import from Geonames, and requires settings access. For each country it removes entries that are no longer in the download and adds the new city zips. This fills the zip lookup from the base_location module with a full list of places.

name: base_location_nuts
summary: Adds NUTS regions, the EU statistical region codes, to partners in four levels from country down to small region. An import wizard under Contacts, Configuration, Localization downloads the official list, and partners get NUTS 1 to NUTS 4 fields. Regions can be flagged Not updatable so the import wizard leaves them alone.

name: base_location_nuts
summary: Imports the European NUTS region list and adds NUTS level 1 to 4 fields to contacts. Regions can be marked Not updatable so the import does not overwrite or delete them. The import can be run from Contacts > Configuration > Localization.

name: base_m2m_custom_field
summary: A technical field type that lets developers create many-to-many relationships with direct access to the link table. This makes it possible to edit those links in their own list view. It has no screens of its own and is used by developers building custom features.

name: base_m2m_custom_field
summary: Technical module that adds a Many2many field type which can point at an existing join table, so a developer can show that table as its own editable list. Business users will not see anything on screen from it directly. It is a building block for other modules.

name: base_maintenance
summary: Adds a few basics to Maintenance teams: a team leader, a description, a search view for teams, and an empty button area on maintenance requests that other modules can fill. It also includes a Maintenance Request report. Team settings show under Maintenance, Configuration, Maintenance Teams.

name: base_maintenance
summary: Adds a team leader and a description to maintenance teams, a search view for teams, and a maintenance request report. It is a base module that other maintenance features build on. Requests also get an empty button area for other modules to fill.

name: base_maintenance_config
summary: Technical module that adds an empty General Settings section to the Maintenance app, so other modules can place their maintenance settings there. On its own it adds no features. The page is found under Maintenance, Configuration, General Settings.

name: base_maintenance_group
summary: Adds Maintenance user access groups, User and Full Access, so you can control who sees the Maintenance menus. Assign them under Settings > Users & Companies > Users in the Access Rights tab. The Equipment Manager group is listed in the same category.

name: base_maintenance_group
summary: Adds a Maintenance security category with User and Full Access groups, next to the standard Equipment Manager group. Assigning one of these groups to a user turns on the Maintenance menus for that user. It is set on the user form under Access Rights.

name: base_menu_visibility_restriction
summary: Hides chosen menu items from users who belong to particular groups, so each user only sees the menus meant for them. Excluded groups are set on each menu item in debug mode, under Settings, Technical, User Interface, Menu Items. It is a simple way to tidy up menus per role.

name: base_menu_visibility_restriction
summary: Lets an administrator hide specific menu items from users who belong to chosen groups. In developer mode, open Settings, Technical, User interface, Menu Items, and fill in Excluded groups on the menu. Users in those groups will no longer see that menu.

name: base_model_restrict_update
summary: Lets admins make a model read-only for most users, with exemptions for chosen groups, or revoke editing rights for a specific user. Configured on the model form and the user form under Settings, Technical. It is a security tool for locking down data.

name: base_model_restrict_update
summary: Lets an administrator make a model read-only for most users, while still allowing chosen groups to edit it. It can also revoke editing rights for a single user, using the Read-only User setting on the user form. Model settings are found under Settings, Technical, Database Structure, Models.

name: base_multi_company
summary: Technical base for multi-company. It changes how company access works so one record can be shared with several chosen companies, not just one company or all of them. It does nothing by itself, and other modules such as product or partner multi-company use it to add company access to their records.

name: base_multi_company
summary: Technical base for multi-company. It changes how company access works so one record can be shared with several chosen companies, not just one company or all of them. It does nothing by itself, and other modules such as product or partner multi-company use it to add company access to their records.

name: base_multi_image
summary: Lets any record, such as a product or partner, hold a gallery of several images instead of one. Images can be managed from Settings, Technical, Multi Images. It is a base module that other apps, such as product image galleries, build on.

name: base_multi_image
summary: Lets any record have a gallery of several images, each with a title, comments and an order. Images are managed under Settings, Technical, Multi images, and other modules such as product images build on it. Developers attach the gallery to their own model by inheriting the owner model.

name: base_multicompany_reporting_currency
summary: Adds a Multicompany Reporting Currency setting in General Settings, so amounts from different companies can be compared in one currency. Each company also gets a reporting amount setting. The module shows no totals itself, and the Sales or CRM add-ons add a Total (Multicompany Reporting Currency) field.

name: base_multicompany_reporting_currency
summary: Adds a Multicompany Reporting Currency setting in General Settings, so amounts from different companies can be compared in one currency. The choice is stored for the whole database and applied to every company's records. The Sales or CRM add-ons then add a Total (Multicompany Reporting Currency) field to their screens.

name: base_name_search_improved
summary: Makes searching in relation fields much more forgiving, so typing words in a different order or missing a middle name still finds the right record. If few results are found, it also searches other fields such as city or phone, which admins can configure per model. This affects dropdown lookups like choosing a customer on a sales order, not the top search bar.

name: base_name_search_improved
summary: Makes the search box on related fields, such as Customer on a sale order, more forgiving. Typing words in a different order or leaving out words still finds the record, and administrators can add extra fields such as city or phone to the search. It is configured per model under Settings, Smart Searches.

name: base_optional_quick_create
summary: Stops the Create quick option from appearing in dropdowns for chosen models, so users must open the full form to add a new record. It is switched on per model under Settings, Technical, Models, Avoid Quick Create. It helps keep records like contacts from being created with incomplete details.

name: base_optional_quick_create
summary: Hides the Quick create shortcut in dropdown lookup fields for models you choose, so users must open the full create form instead. It is turned on per model with the Avoid quick create option in the model settings, under Settings, Technical, Database Structure, Models.

name: base_partition
summary: A technical helper that splits a set of records into groups by a field value, such as separating paid and unpaid invoices in code. It adds a partition method to every model. Users see no change; it is for developers.

name: base_partition
summary: Technical helper that adds a partition method to every model, splitting a set of records into groups by a field or a function. Developers use it in code, and end users see no screens from it. It is a building block for other modules.

name: base_partner_company_group
summary: Adds a Company group field to contacts, so related companies can be grouped, searched and filtered together. The group is set on a company contact and passed down to its contacts, and the form lists the group's members. Sales, CRM and invoicing need the matching add-on modules to show the group there.

name: base_partner_company_group
summary: Adds a Company Group field to companies, which is also passed on to their contacts, so contacts can be searched and grouped by company group. Leads, orders and invoices need the CRM, Sales or Accounting company group modules instead. This is the base module for company groups.

name: base_partner_merge_user_consolidation
summary: When merging duplicate contacts, also tidies up the user accounts linked to them. The most recently active user is kept and linked to the merged contact, and the others are archived with a changed login so they cannot sign in. It works from the Merge Contacts wizard.

name: base_partner_merge_user_consolidation
summary: When you merge duplicate contacts that each have a login, this keeps the user who logged in most recently, keeps that account active and linked to the merged contact, and archives the others with scrambled logins so they cannot sign in. It runs inside the standard Merge Contacts wizard. It helps avoid multiple logins and confusing access after a merge.

name: base_partner_sequence
summary: Gives each new customer a reference code taken from a sequence, which is set as the default on new partners. The reference is managed on the company contact and copied to its contacts. Addresses such as delivery and invoice contacts do not get a reference.

name: base_partner_sequence
summary: Fills in an automatic customer code (the reference field) on new company contacts, using a sequence you configure. The code is managed from the main company contact and shared with its contacts, while shipping and invoice addresses get no code. A setting can make the code read-only for everyone.

name: base_phone
summary: Cleans up phone numbers on contacts and users, converting them to the standard international format when saved, based on the company's country. It also adds a Number not found record for unknown incoming callers and a tool to reformat existing numbers in bulk. It is a base for telephony connectors such as the Asterisk one.

name: base_phone
summary: Cleans up phone numbers on contacts and users, converting them to the standard international format when saved, based on the company's country. It also adds a Number not found record for unknown incoming callers and a tool to reformat existing numbers in bulk. It is a base for telephony connectors such as the Asterisk one.

name: base_portal_type
summary: Lets administrators create groups for portal users, so customers and vendors using the portal can get different views and features. Groups in the portal type category appear on the user form for portal users. It is a technical base for portal setups.

name: base_portal_type
summary: Lets an administrator create groups for portal (external) users, so different kinds of external users such as vendors and customers can be told apart. Portal groups can then control which views and features each type sees. Groups are created in the portal type category and assigned on the user form for Portal users.

name: base_product_mass_addition
summary: Abstract base that lets other apps show a product grid where users enter quantities for many products at once, instead of adding order lines one by one. It cannot be used on its own. It is built into quick-entry features such as sale_quick, purchase_quick and stock_picking_quick.

name: base_product_merge
summary: Merges duplicate products or product templates into one destination product. Select the products in a list, use the Actions menu and choose Merge products, pick the product to keep, and the others are merged into it. It helps clean up a product catalog that has the same item listed more than once.

name: base_remote
summary: Technical module that records every external connection to Odoo by hostname and IP address, and keeps the last IP seen for each. The list is viewed under Settings, Remotes, and other modules use it to check remote configurations. It has no business screens of its own.

name: base_remote
summary: Keeps a list of the network addresses that have connected to Odoo, storing each hostname, its last IP address and whether it is inside the company network. The list is viewable under Settings, Remotes. It is a technical helper for other modules and for security checks.

name: base_repair_config
summary: Technical module that adds an empty General Settings section to the Repair app, so other modules can add their repair settings there. On its own it adds no features. The page is found under Repair, Configuration, Settings.

name: base_repair_config
summary: Technical base module that adds an empty General Settings section to the Repair app, so other add-ons can place their repair-related settings there. It adds no settings of its own. Users see it as Repair > Configuration > Settings, where nothing new appears until another module extends it.

name: base_report_auto_create_qweb
summary: Technical helper for report developers. When a report is created under Settings > Technical > Reports, Odoo also creates an empty QWeb template and the links between them, so the developer does not have to wire them up by hand. Reports also get a Duplicate action that copies a report with a suffix such as 'copy'.

name: base_report_to_label_printer
summary: Lets a report be flagged as a label report so it prints to a label printer instead of the general one. Each user can have a default label printer on their user record. The base report-to-printer module must be set up first.

name: base_report_to_label_printer
summary: Lets a report be flagged as a label report so it prints to a label printer instead of the general one. Each user can have a default label printer on their user record. The base report-to-printer module must be set up first.

name: base_report_to_printer
summary: Lets users send Odoo reports straight to a printer instead of downloading a PDF. Printers, paper trays and print behaviour can be set globally, per user, per report, or per user and report, under Settings > Printing. The actual printer connection comes from a backend add-on. Printer trays and per-report defaults are configured in the same place, and each user needs the Printing / Print User access right to see the print menu.

name: base_report_to_printer
summary: Lets users send Odoo reports straight to a printer instead of downloading a PDF. Printers, paper trays and print behaviour can be set globally, per user, per report, or per user and report, under Settings > Printing. The actual printer connection comes from a backend add-on. Printer trays and per-report defaults are configured in the same place, and each user needs the Printing / Print User access right to see the print menu.

name: base_report_to_printer
summary: Core framework that lets Odoo reports go to physical printers without tying them to one printing protocol. Printing behaviour (download a PDF or print) can be set globally, per user, per report, or per user and report, under Settings > Printing. Actual printer connections come from backend add-ons such as base_report_to_printer_cups.

name: base_report_to_printer_cups
summary: Connects the printing framework to CUPS print servers. You add a CUPS server under Settings > Printing > Servers, click Update Printers to load its printers and paper trays, and reports can then print directly to them instead of downloading a PDF. A Print Test Page action checks that a printer works.

name: base_report_to_printer_mail
summary: Small add-on that stops a report from going to a selected printer when it is triggered from an email template. Those reports are still sent by email as usual. It only changes how mail templates behave, with no new screens.

name: base_report_to_printer_mail
summary: Small add-on that stops a report from going to a selected printer when it is triggered from an email template. Those reports are still sent by email as usual. It only changes how mail templates behave, with no new screens.

name: base_report_to_printer_qztray
summary: Lets reports print from the user's own computer through the QZ Tray helper app, instead of through the Odoo server. It suits point of sale, kiosks, or any setup where the server cannot reach the printers. Printers are created with the QZ Tray backend under Settings > Technical > Printing > Printers.

name: base_report_to_printer_websocket
summary: Sends print jobs over the Odoo bus (WebSocket) to a small client program on a user's computer, which forwards the PDF to a local printer. No print server is needed. Each printer is tied to one Odoo user and is set up under Settings > Printing > Printers with the WebSocket backend.

name: base_rest
summary: Technical framework for building custom REST APIs on top of Odoo, so outside systems can call business logic without using the raw XML-RPC interface. It generates Swagger documentation for the services. This version is deprecated from Odoo 16 onward, and its notes recommend the FastAPI migration module instead. Business users see nothing new in the menus.

name: base_rest
summary: Technical framework for building custom REST APIs on top of Odoo, so outside systems can call business logic without using the raw XML-RPC interface. It generates Swagger documentation for the services. This version is deprecated from Odoo 16 onward, and its notes recommend the FastAPI migration module instead. Business users see nothing new in the menus.

name: base_rest_auth_api_key
summary: Technical add-on that makes the API key login method appear in the generated Swagger/OpenAPI documentation for REST services built on base_rest. It adds no screens or business features. Only developers exposing REST APIs with API key security need it.

name: base_rest_auth_api_key
summary: Technical add-on that makes the API key login method appear in the generated Swagger/OpenAPI documentation for REST services built on base_rest. It adds no screens or business features. Only developers exposing REST APIs with API key security need it.

name: base_rest_datamodel
summary: Technical add-on that lets REST API endpoints built on base_rest accept and return DataModel objects as inputs and outputs. It is for developers writing custom REST services and has no business screens.

name: base_rest_demo
summary: Demo add-on with sample REST services built on base_rest, showing developers how to write self-documenting APIs. Its Swagger documentation page at /api-docs lists the sample endpoints. Meant for testing and learning, not for live business use.

name: base_rest_pydantic
summary: Technical add-on that lets REST API endpoints built on base_rest accept and return Pydantic objects, a Python data-validation library. It is for developers writing custom REST services and has no business screens.

name: base_rest_pydantic
summary: Technical add-on that lets REST API endpoints built on base_rest accept and return Pydantic objects, a Python data-validation library. It is for developers writing custom REST services and has no business screens.

name: base_revision
summary: Technical base module that gives other models a revision history, so a document can be copied into a numbered revision (such as -1, -2) while the old versions are kept and archived. It has no screens of its own. Sale Order Revision uses it, adding a New copy of Quotation button on cancelled quotations and a list of previous revisions on the sale order.

name: base_revision
summary: A base feature for keeping earlier versions of a document when it is revised, such as a sale order that is copied as a new revision with an incremented number. Old revisions are archived and listed on the document. It does nothing alone; the sale order revision module is the example that uses it.

name: base_rule_visibility_restriction
summary: Adds an Excluded Groups field to record rules, so a rule can be skipped for users in certain groups. This helps when one group must be exempt from a restriction that applies to others. Developers set it under Settings > Technical > Security > Record Rules with developer mode on.

name: base_search_custom_field_filter
summary: Lets administrators define their own filters on the search bar of any list or search view, based on a field on the record or on a related record. Once set up, the filter appears for regular users in the search dropdown. It is configured under Settings > Technical > User Interface > Custom Field Filters, and the demo adds a Language filter on Contacts.

name: base_search_custom_field_filter
summary: Lets admins define extra search filters on fields of a document or related documents, which then appear in the search bar for all users. Filters are created under Settings, Technical, User Interface, Custom Field Filters. A demo filter is included to show how it works.

name: base_search_fuzzy
summary: Technical add-on that enables fuzzy (approximate) text search using the PostgreSQL trigram extension, so a search for 'Jon Miller' can still find 'John Miller'. Trigram indexes are created under Settings > Technical > Database Structure > Trigram Index. On its own it does not change normal search, so other add-ons must use the fuzzy operator.

name: base_search_fuzzy
summary: Adds fuzzy text matching to the database so searches can find near-spelling matches, such as John Smit for John Smith. Admins can add trigram indexes on text fields under Settings, Database Structure, Trigram Index. It is a technical base module used by developers and does not change existing searches.

name: base_search_mail_content
summary: Adds a Message Content search field to any record with a chatter, so you can find records by what was written in their messages. Searches cover the subject, body, sender, reply-to and record name. It is most useful on helpdesk tickets and project issues that have long conversations.

name: base_search_mail_content
summary: Adds a Message Content search field to any record with a chatter, so users can find records by words in their emails and notes. It is useful for finding a project issue or helpdesk ticket by something said in its conversation. The field appears in the search bar of models such as Contacts.

name: base_sequence_default
summary: Technical utility that lets a sequence fill in a default text value on a new record, such as an automatic reference code on a custom field. Setup needs developer mode, and the field is chosen from its tooltip on the form. Empty fields (or fields set to '-' when required) get the next number on save.

name: base_sequence_option
summary: Lets admins set up alternate numbering for documents, so for example customer invoices for one customer or region use a different number sequence than the default. Rules are matched on document values and configured under Settings, Technical, Sequences, Manage Sequence Options. It is a base module that document-specific add-ons build on.

name: base_sequence_option
summary: Base technical module that lets a document type use its own numbering sequence depending on the record's values, for example a different invoice numbering per customer region. Setup is under Settings > Technical > Sequences & Identifiers > Manage Sequence Options. It does nothing by itself; the extension modules for purchases, invoices and others provide the actual document types.

name: base_sparse_field_list_support
summary: A technical helper that lets list values be stored in a serialized field and read back correctly. It is for developers and has no screens for users.

name: base_sparse_field_list_support
summary: Technical module that lets list values be stored in a serialized field, extending the base_sparse_field module. Nothing shows up for business users. Developers use it when a field needs to hold a list rather than a single value.

name: base_substate
summary: A base feature for adding sub-statuses within a main status, such as In Negotiation, Won or Lost under a quotation, and optionally sending an email when one is reached. It does nothing alone; app modules like purchase substate use it. Users see the sub-status on the document.

name: base_substate
summary: Technical base module that lets you define custom sub-statuses (for example "In negotiation", "Won" and "Lost") that refine a document's main state, such as a sale quotation. It can also send an email when a sub-status is reached. It is not useful on its own; an application module such as purchase_substate is needed to show the sub-status on a document.

name: base_technical_features
summary: Lets employees reach technical menus and fields without switching on debug mode. Each user can tick a "Technical features" preference to keep that access permanently, and the preference is already on for the administrator after install. It shows up in the user's preferences and in the menus and views marked as technical.

name: base_technical_features
summary: Gives users a Technical features preference that unlocks technical menus and views without turning on debug mode. It is switched on by default for all users at install time. It is used by administrators and developers who need technical screens day to day.

name: base_technical_features
summary: Lets employees reach technical menus and fields without switching on debug mode. Each user can tick a "Technical features" preference (with a "Show Technical Features" option) to keep that access permanently, and the administrator has it on after install. It shows up in the user's preferences and in the menus and views marked as technical.

name: base_technical_user
summary: Adds a Technical User field on the company form (a tab on the company record) so a dedicated user can be set for background or batch processes. The intended setup is an inactive user with the groups that process needs, so nobody logs in with it. Developers can use the configured user from code, and it appears on Settings > Companies.

name: base_technical_user
summary: Lets a company be linked to an inactive technical user that background and batch processes run under. A helper method lets developers run code as that user, or as the superuser if none is set. The setting appears in a tab on the company form under Settings, Companies.

name: base_temporary_action
summary: A technical helper that lets developers mark actions as temporary so they are removed automatically after about an hour. It does nothing visible on its own. Used by developers when a short-lived window or action is needed.

name: base_territory
summary: Technical base module. It defines a territory structure of regions, districts and branches, each with a manager, and lets countries and ZIP codes be assigned to territories. Records are created under Settings, Users and Companies and are used by field service and sales.

name: base_territory
summary: Lets you define territories, branches, districts and regions, each with a manager, for sales and field service planning. Territories can be linked to ZIP codes and countries, and countries get a territory and region field. Setup is under Settings > Users & Companies.

name: base_tier_validation
summary: A base feature for requiring one or more people to approve a document before it can be used, in ordered tiers such as a manager and then a director. Admins define tiers under Settings, Technical, Tier Validations, Tier Definition, and approvals are shown on the document. It does nothing alone; apps like purchase tier validation use it.

name: base_tier_validation
summary: Base engine for multi-step approvals (tiers) that can be added to any document type, such as purchase or sale orders. It does not add an approval process by itself; you define tiers under Settings > Technical > Tier Validations > Tier Definition, and a Validate or Reject flow then appears on the supported documents. It is a technical base for developers and other modules.

name: base_tier_validation_board
summary: Adds a Tier Review board with form, list, kanban, calendar, pivot, graph and search views under the Boards menu. It lets you see approvals across documents and open the original document from a review. It depends on the spreadsheet dashboard module.

name: base_tier_validation_confirm_auth
summary: Requires an approver to re-enter their login password before approving or rejecting a tier review. It is turned on per tier definition with a Require Authentication checkbox. It adds an extra safeguard to approvals.

name: base_tier_validation_correction
summary: Lets a user with the Tier Review Correction role reassign pending approvals from one reviewer to another, for example when someone is away. Corrections are created under Settings > Technical > Tier Validation > Tier Review Correction, where you pick the document model and find the affected pending reviews. Reassigning reviewers is the only correction type available today.

name: base_tier_validation_correction
summary: Lets a user with the Tier Review Correction role change who the reviewer is on a pending approval, for example when the original approver is away. Corrections are made under Settings, Technical, Tier Validation, Tier Review Correction. It keeps approvals moving without cancelling the document.

name: base_tier_validation_definition_server_action
summary: Lets a tier definition decide whether approval is needed by running a server action that sets a true or false variable. The action runs against the same model as the definition, so the rule can depend on the document's data. It is set on each Tier Definition by choosing the Server Action option.

name: base_tier_validation_formula
summary: Lets admins write Python code to decide when a tier applies and who the reviewers are, rather than only using a domain filter. The formula is chosen on each tier definition under Settings, Technical, Tier Validations. It gives approval rules more flexibility.

name: base_tier_validation_forward
summary: Adds a Forward option so a reviewer who does not want to decide can pass the approval to another user. A new review is inserted for the next user, who can then approve or reject. It is switched on per tier definition with the Allow Forward checkbox.

name: base_tier_validation_forward
summary: Lets an approver forward a pending approval to another person when they do not want to decide themselves, with the new reviewer added to the approval chain. The option is enabled per tier definition with Allow Forward. Users see a Forward button next to Approve and Reject.

name: base_tier_validation_report
summary: Adds two approval reports to the Dashboard app: My Reviews and All Reviews, each split into pending, approved and rejected. Use them to see what is waiting on you or what the whole company is approving. It needs the tier validation engine to be in use.

name: base_tier_validation_server_action
summary: Lets a tier definition run a server action automatically when the tier is approved or rejected, such as sending a notification or updating a field. Tiers can also be validated automatically by a scheduled job when a condition is met. Set up on each tier definition under Settings, Technical, Tier Validations.

name: base_tier_validation_server_action
summary: Runs a chosen server action when a tier is approved or rejected, for example to send a notification or update a record. It can also auto-validate a tier through a scheduled job when its condition passes, using the job's system user or the single matching reviewer. These options are set on each Tier Definition.

name: base_tier_validation_waiting
summary: Adds a Waiting status to approval reviews, so a later reviewer only becomes Pending once the earlier tier is done. The next review moves to Pending automatically. You can also tick Notify Reviewers on reaching Pending on a tier definition to email the reviewer at that point.

name: base_time_parameter
summary: Lets admins store settings whose value changes over time, such as a tax rate or a fee that starts on a given date. Each parameter has dated versions, and the correct value for a date is picked automatically. It is found under Settings, Technical, Time Parameters.

name: base_time_window
summary: Technical base that gives models a time window: a start and end time of day plus the weekdays it applies to, with a check for overlapping windows. It has no screens of its own and is meant for developers to use in other modules. An example is in the test_base_time_window module.

name: base_time_window
summary: A technical base for records that are only valid during certain time windows, such as opening hours or delivery slots on specific weekdays. It checks that windows do not overlap for the same parent record. Developers use it in other modules; users do not see it on its own.

name: base_transaction_id
summary: Adds a Transaction ID field to sales orders and invoices. The value set on the sale order is copied to the invoice, including invoices created from deliveries, which helps match bank payments from e-commerce to the right partner. It depends on the sale module and shows on the sale order and invoice forms.

name: base_transaction_id
summary: Adds a Transaction ID field to sales orders and invoices. The value set on the sale order is copied to the invoice, including invoices created from deliveries, which helps match bank payments from e-commerce to the right partner. It depends on the sale module and shows on the sale order and invoice forms.

name: base_ubl
summary: Technical base for the UBL (Universal Business Language) XML standard, with the methods to generate and read UBL files. It does nothing visible by itself; other modules such as purchase order UBL, sale order import and invoice import depend on it. Use it when you need electronic business documents in UBL format.

name: base_ubl
summary: Technical base for the UBL (Universal Business Language) XML standard, with the methods to generate and read UBL files. It does nothing visible by itself; other modules such as purchase order UBL, sale order import and invoice import depend on it. This version also pulls in UNECE code lists, tax and VAT helpers, and PDF support.

name: base_ubl_generate
summary: Technical module that adds the methods to create UBL XML files from Odoo documents. It has no screens of its own and is used by other modules, such as purchase order UBL, that send UBL files out. Install it only as a dependency of such a module.

name: base_ubl_parse
summary: Technical module that adds the methods to read UBL XML files. It has no screens of its own and is used by import modules such as sale order import UBL and invoice import UBL. Install it as a dependency when you need to load UBL documents into Odoo.

name: base_ubl_payment
summary: Small add-on to the UBL base that adds the PaymentMeans block to generated UBL documents, so the payment method is included in the XML. It depends on the UNECE payment code module and the banking payment export module. It has no screens of its own.

name: base_ubl_payment_banking_mandate
summary: Glue module that adds the banking mandate to the UBL payment means when the payment code is 49 or 59 (direct debit). It connects the UBL payment block with the banking mandate module. It has no screens of its own.

name: base_unece
summary: Technical base that stores UNECE standard code lists, such as units of measure, payment means, transport modes, packaging and tax codes. The lists are kept under Settings > Technical > Parameters > UNECE Code Lists. Other EDI and e-invoicing modules use these codes.

name: base_unece
summary: Technical base that stores UNECE standard code lists, such as units of measure, payment means, transport modes, packaging and tax codes. The lists are kept under Settings > Technical > Parameters > UNECE Code Lists. Other EDI and e-invoicing modules use these codes.

name: base_url
summary: A technical base that gives records clean, stable web addresses based on a key instead of a database ID, and redirects old addresses when a key changes. It was built for online shops that need unique links per record. Users see nothing by default; developers use it in other modules.

name: base_user_chatter
summary: Adds the chatter (messages, notes and activity log) to the user form, so you can record notes or actions about a user. You will find it on the user record under Settings > Users & Companies > Users.

name: base_user_effective_permissions
summary: Shows a combined view of a user's access rights and record rules for each model, with the rule conditions written out. It is useful for checking what a user can really see or change. It is opened from the user form in developer mode.

name: base_user_effective_permissions
summary: In developer mode, an Effective permissions button appears on the user form under Settings > Users & Companies. It shows, per model, the combined access rights and record rules that apply to that user, with the rule conditions expanded. Use it to review or audit who can see and change what.

name: base_user_empty_password
summary: Adds a wizard that clears the password of selected users, so they must sign in another way, such as through single sign-on. Use it to move users off local Odoo passwords. It is a technical administration tool.

name: base_user_locale
summary: Lets a company, and each user, override the date format, time format, first day of the week, and decimal and thousands separators. Company values are set under Settings > General Settings in the Locale section, and user values in each user's preferences. The result is that numbers and dates display in the format each person expects.

name: base_user_locale
summary: Lets each company, and each user, override regional display settings such as date format, time format, first day of the week, and decimal and thousands separators. Company settings are under Settings, General Settings, Locale, and user settings are in each user's preferences. It changes how numbers and dates look for the people it is set for.

name: base_user_role
summary: Lets you group technical access rights into named roles, then assign roles to users. Roles can have start and end dates, and a user's groups are kept in line with their roles. Use it to manage many users without juggling individual groups.

name: base_user_role
summary: Lets you define functional roles that bundle several security groups, then assign those roles to users, optionally for a date range. Each user's groups stay in sync with their roles, so access is managed in one place. Roles are created under Settings > Users > Roles and can be shown as an overview of role holders.

name: base_user_role_activity
summary: Creates a reminder activity when a user's role assignment is close to ending, 30 days before by default. The activity is attached to the user's partner record, and it is removed if the end date changes. It builds on the user roles module.

name: base_user_role_company
summary: Add-on that limits user roles to specific companies. On the user form, each role line gets a Company column, so a role such as Sales Manager can be set to apply to Company A only. When a user selects several companies in the top-right company switcher, only roles valid for all of the selected companies stay active, and the user's security groups are recalculated to match.

name: base_user_role_company
summary: Makes a role apply only when the selected companies allow it. A company-specific role is active only if it is valid for every company currently selected, and the user's groups update when the company selection changes. It is set on the user's role lines.

name: base_user_role_history
summary: Keeps an audit trail of changes to user roles. Each time a role is added, changed or removed on a user, a history line records the old and new role, dates and active flag, plus who made the change. The history is opened from a smart button on the user form, and the user record shows the date of the last role change.

name: base_user_role_history
summary: Keeps a log of every change to a user's roles, recording what changed, who made the change, and the old and new dates. A smart button on the user form opens the history. Use it to audit role changes.

name: base_user_role_history
summary: Keeps an audit trail of changes to user roles. Each time a role is added, changed or removed on a user, a history line records what changed and who made the change. The history is opened from a smart button on the user form, and the user record shows the date of the last role modification.

name: base_user_role_profile
summary: Adds profiles on top of user roles, so a user can switch between permission sets from the top bar. Each role can be linked to a profile, and roles without a profile always apply. Use it to simplify menus or limit editing in certain work modes.

name: base_user_show_email
summary: Small display change for users whose login is different from their email address. On the user form in Settings > Users & Companies > Users, the login field is labelled Login instead of Email and the email field is shown separately, and the user list shows the email next to the login.

name: base_user_show_email
summary: Separates the login and email fields on the user form, labelling the first one Login and showing Email as its own field. The user list also shows the email next to the login. Use it when logins are not email addresses.

name: base_user_signature
summary: Adds a Signature image field to user records, so each user can store a digital signature. It is set under Settings > Users & Companies > Users on the user form. This is a technical base module that other documents can use.

name: base_user_signature
summary: Adds a Signature image field to each user, so a digital signature can be uploaded and stored against the user. It is found on the user form in Settings > Users & Companies > Users. This module only adds the field; where the signature gets printed depends on other modules.

name: base_vat_optional_vies
summary: Makes the EU VIES online VAT check optional and softer. When VIES checking is on, a VAT number that is valid for its country is accepted even if VIES does not confirm it, and the partner shows a 'VIES validation passed' flag. That flag can be used to show the VAT number with or without its country prefix on invoices. The VIES setting is in Settings > Accounting > Verify VAT Numbers.

name: base_view_inheritance_extension
summary: A technical add-on that extends how view customizations are written, adding extra operators for editing dictionaries, text and domains inside views. It is for developers who customize screens, and nothing changes for end users.

name: base_view_inheritance_extension
summary: Technical add-on for developers who customize screen layouts (views) in Odoo. It adds extra operators for view inheritance, such as changing a Python dictionary value (for example a context), adding text before or after an existing element, and adding domain conditions joined with AND or OR. End users do not interact with it directly.

name: base_wamas_ubl
summary: Technical base module for the WAMAS and UBL electronic document formats in the EDI repository. It holds the conversion logic between WAMAS telegram files and UBL XML in both directions. It adds two wizards, one to check an uploaded WAMAS file and one to simulate its conversion and produce the output file.

name: base_warn_option
summary: A base feature that gives warning and blocking messages standard options for who can see them and how they are used, so warnings stay consistent across apps. Warning options are kept under the settings for warnings. It is a technical base that other modules use for their pop-up messages.

name: base_write_diff
summary: Technical helper for developers that stops Odoo from writing fields whose values would not change. When code updates records, only the values that are really different from the current ones are passed on, which can avoid unnecessary processing and recalculation during saves. End users see no change on screen.

name: bc3_importer
summary: Imports construction quotations from a BC3 file (the budget exchange format used in construction). A wizard reads the file and builds the lines of a sale order linked to a project, and can create products that do not exist yet. The sale order and its lines then carry the BC3 header and code information.
keywords: import sale order lines from file

name: bi_sql_editor
summary: Lets an administrator write a custom SQL query and turn it into a new reporting view, with its own menu, action and graph or tree views. The view can be materialized and refreshed by a scheduled task, and access can be limited to chosen groups and a domain. It appears under the Dashboards SQL Reports menu and is intended for technical users.

name: bi_sql_editor
summary: Lets an administrator write a custom SQL query and turn its result into a new report under Dashboards > SQL Reports, with pivot, graph and list views. The module generates the model, fields, menu, action and graph view from the query, and can store the result as a materialized view that a scheduled job refreshes. Intended for technical users who know SQL and Odoo models; access is by default for the SQL Request / User group.

name: bi_view_editor
summary: Drag-and-drop report builder for users with little technical knowledge. Under Dashboards > Custom BI Views, a user picks business objects and fields in the Query Builder tab, links them, and gets tree, graph and pivot views. Creating BI views is limited to the BI View Editor Manager group, and this version depends on the Spreadsheet Dashboard module.

name: bi_view_editor
summary: Drag-and-drop report builder for users with little technical knowledge. Under the Dashboards menu, a user picks business objects and fields in the Query Builder tab, links them, and gets tree, graph and pivot views. Creating BI views is limited to the BI View Editor Manager group, and this version does not depend on the Spreadsheet Dashboard module.

name: bi_view_editor_spreadsheet_dashboard
summary: Technical glue module that auto-installs when BI View Editor and Spreadsheet Dashboard are both installed. It moves the BI View Editor menu items from the legacy Dashboards menu to the Spreadsheet Dashboard menu. It adds no new features of its own.

name: bi_view_editor_spreadsheet_dashboard
summary: Technical glue module that auto-installs when BI View Editor and Spreadsheet Dashboard are both installed. It moves the BI View Editor menu items from the legacy Dashboards menu to the Spreadsheet Dashboard menu. It adds no new features of its own.

name: bookstore_mgmt
summary: Bookstore add-on that treats books as products. On a product, tick Is a book, then set its author, editorial (publisher), genre and year of edition. The authors, editorials and genres are simple lists that can be picked on the product form.

name: bookstore_mgmt_google_books_api
summary: Adds an Import book data button on book products. The button looks up the book by its barcode, which should be the ISBN-10 or ISBN-13, through the Google Books API and updates the product with the returned book information. Requires the Bookstore Management add-on.

name: brand
summary: Base add-on for brand modules. It adds a Brands list under Settings > Users & Companies > Brands, a brand use level setting in General Settings, and an abstract brand mixin that other modules inherit to put a brand on their records. On its own it changes little on screen; the visible brand fields come from the branding modules installed on top.

name: brand
summary: Base add-on for brand modules. It adds a Brands list under Settings > Users & Companies > Brands, a brand use level setting in General Settings, and an abstract brand mixin that other modules inherit to put a brand on their records. It also adds a brand required flag on the mixin, and on its own changes little on screen.

name: brand_external_report_layout
summary: Gives each brand its own look on printed external reports (PDF). A brand can have its own logo, report header and footer, font, colours, paper format and company details, selected under Settings > Users & Companies > Brands. Printing a report from a branded record then uses that brand's layout.

name: brand_external_report_layout
summary: Gives each brand its own look on printed external reports (PDF). A brand can have its own logo, report header and footer, font, colours, paper format and company details, selected under Settings > Users & Companies > Brands. Printing a report from a branded record then uses that brand's layout.

name: bus_alt_connection
summary: A technical add-on for installations that use PgBouncer as a database connection pooler. It lets the Odoo bus (live notifications) connect directly to the database with its own settings. Only administrators running this kind of server setup need it.

name: bus_alt_connection
summary: Technical infrastructure module for hosting teams. It lets Odoo connect to PostgreSQL through the PgBouncer connection pooler, so connections are shared across workers and instances. The direct database host and port are set with environment variables or in the Odoo configuration file. Nothing changes on screen for users.

name: business_requirement
summary: Core module for business requirements (BR), which record a customer or internal need. Each requirement holds the customer story, scenario, gap, test case, terms and conditions, categories and state, and the menu sits under the Business Requirements app. It is the base that the other business requirement add-ons build on.

name: business_requirement_crm
summary: Lets a salesperson turn a CRM opportunity into a business requirement. On a lead, the Convert to Requirement button opens a wizard that creates the requirement and links it back to the lead, and the lead shows a count of its requirements.

name: business_requirement_crm
summary: Adds a Create Business Requirement button on CRM leads and opportunities. The wizard fills in a description and the customer history from the lead, creates the requirement and links it back to the lead, which then shows a count of its business requirements.

name: business_requirement_deliverable
summary: Adds deliverables and resources to a business requirement. Deliverable lines are the products and services the customer receives, priced from the customer's pricelist, and each one can have resource lines that carry the internal cost. Sections group the deliverables, and totals and revenue show on the requirement. A partner estimation pricelist and a master project can also be set up.

name: business_requirement_rice
summary: Ranks business requirements with the RICE scoring model (Reach, Impact, Confidence, Effort). Fill in the RICE tab on a requirement and the score is computed and stored, so you can sort or group the list by it. The existing priority field is left alone, and a Scored filter hides requirements nobody has estimated yet.

name: business_requirement_sale
summary: Creates sales quotations from a business requirement. Open a requirement and click Create Quotation, then pick the sections and deliverables to quote in the wizard, and each chosen deliverable becomes a sales order line. The quotation links back to the requirement, and the requirement lists its sales orders.
