name: calendar_event_description_layout
summary: The calendar event form has a small Description box, which gets cramped when people write long notes. This module moves the Description field onto its own tab so there is room to write and read it. It shows up on the calendar event form in the Calendar app.

name: calendar_event_description_layout
summary: The calendar event form has a small Description box, which gets cramped when people write long notes. This module moves the Description field onto its own tab so there is room to write and read it. It shows up on the calendar event form in the Calendar app.

name: calendar_event_link_base
summary: This is a technical base module with no new screens of its own. It adds an abstract mixin that lets any other Odoo model be linked to calendar events, with a count of linked events and a button that opens them. Developers use it to add a calendar events button to the form of their own models.

name: calendar_event_multi_company
summary: In a multi-company database, this module adds a Company field to calendar events, so each meeting belongs to one company. Users can then see and manage events per company. It appears on the calendar event form in the Calendar app.

name: calendar_event_type_color
summary: This module colors events in the calendar view using the color set on each event type. If an event has several categories, its color comes from the first one in the category order. Users set the color on the event type list view to make calendar entries easier to tell apart.

name: calendar_event_type_color
summary: This module colors events in the calendar view using the color set on each event type. If an event has several categories, its color comes from the first one in the category order. Users set the color on the event type list view to make calendar entries easier to tell apart.

name: calendar_event_type_multi_company
summary: In a multi-company database, this module adds a Company field to calendar event types, so each event type can be limited to one company. This keeps the list of meeting types for each company separate. It shows up on the event type setup in the Calendar app.

name: calendar_export_ics
summary: This module adds a wizard that exports Odoo calendar events to an .ics file, the standard calendar format used by Outlook, Google Calendar and Apple Calendar. You can export everything, or only events up to an end date you choose. It is started from Configuration > Export to ICS File in the Calendar app.

name: calendar_import_ics
summary: This module adds a wizard that imports an .ics calendar file into Odoo, creating events from the summary, start date, end date and UID of each entry. You can limit the import to a date range, and optionally remove older events that came from a previous import. It is started from Configuration > Import ICS File in the Calendar app.

name: calendar_monthly_multi
summary: This module extends monthly recurring events so they can repeat on several set days, such as the 5th and 15th, or on a pattern like the first weekday of the month. Recurrence can use all days, weekdays, weekend days or a custom day list. It is set on the event form in the Calendar app by choosing Recurrent, then Monthly.

name: calendar_public_holiday
summary: This module keeps a list of public holidays by year and country, with the date of each holiday. Holidays that move from year to year can be flagged as variable dates, and a new year can be created by copying an existing set. Holidays are managed from the Calendar app under Public Holidays.

name: carrier_account_environment
summary: This is a technical module for shipping setups. It moves the delivery carrier account settings (such as API credentials) out of the database and into server configuration files, so production and test servers can use different values. Odoo reads the values for each environment from those files, so no database edits are needed when moving between environments.

name: carrier_account_environment
summary: This is a technical module for shipping setups. It moves the delivery carrier account settings (such as API credentials) out of the database and into server configuration files, so production and test servers can use different values. Odoo reads the values for each environment from those files, so no database edits are needed when moving between environments.

name: chained_swapper
summary: Lets a field value, such as the delivery address on a confirmed sales order, be changed and automatically passed on to linked records like its delivery orders, with rules that can block the change when a linked record is already validated. Admins define the swaps under Settings, Field Swaps, and users run them from the Action menu of a list. It should be used carefully because a wrong setup can leave data inconsistent.

name: cmis
summary: This is a technical base module for connecting Odoo to a CMIS document server, a standard used by enterprise content management systems. It lets an administrator create a CMIS backend with the server location, username, password and a starting folder for writing files. Other modules build the actual document sync on top of it.

name: cms_form
summary: This is a developer framework for building front-end forms on the Odoo website or customer portal. It generates create, edit, search and multi-step wizard forms, and their web routes, for any Odoo model from its field definitions. It is aimed at web developers and does not add a menu for end users.

name: cms_info
summary: This is a technical base module for building a website content system on top of Odoo. It gives website records standard web addresses for create, search, edit, delete and copy, and helper checks for whether the current user owns or can edit a record. Developers use it as a foundation for their own website content modules.

name: cms_status_message
summary: This is a technical module that adds status messages to the website and portal. After a user submits a form or completes an action, a message such as Success, Info, Warning or Error appears as an alert. Messages stack one after another and fade away by default after 8 seconds, and developers set them from Python code.

name: commission
summary: This module handles sales commissions for agents. You can define commission types as a fixed percentage or as percentage bands, assign agents to customers, and create settlements that total the commissions owed for a period. The commission base can be net margin or gross sales line amount, and there is a settlement report grouped by date. It appears in the Commissions app and on customer contact forms.

name: commission
summary: This module handles sales commissions for agents. You can define commission types as a fixed percentage or as percentage bands, assign agents to customers, and create settlements that total the commissions owed for a period. The commission base can be net margin or gross sales line amount, and there is a settlement report grouped by date. It appears in the Commissions app and on customer contact forms.

name: commission_delegated_partner
summary: This module lets an agent's commission invoices be issued to a different partner, such as a company that handles billing for the agent. You set the delegated partner on the agent's record, and the settlement then uses that partner on the invoice. It appears under Sales > Commission Management > Agents.

name: commission_formula
summary: This module lets you calculate agent commissions with a formula instead of a fixed percentage or bands. You pick the formula commission type on the commission setup, and the formula text sets the amount. It is found under Commission > Configuration > Commission Types.

name: commission_formula_oca
summary: This is the OCA version of the commission formula module. It lets you calculate agent commissions with a formula, set by choosing the formula commission type under Commission Types. It builds on the OCA commission module instead of the standard commission module.

name: commission_oca
summary: This is the OCA version of the sales commission module. It lets you define agents and their commission types (fixed percentage or bands), assign agents to customers, and create settlements for a period. The commission base can be net margin or gross line amount, and the settings are under Commissions > Configuration. It is an alternative to the standard commission module, not an add-on to it.

name: company_default_partner_pricelist
summary: When a customer has no pricelist set, Odoo normally guesses one from the customer's country. This module lets you set a default pricelist on each company, which is used for customers without their own pricelist. You set it on the company form under General Settings > Companies.

name: company_dependent_flag
summary: This is a technical module for website styling. It adds a CSS class to every company-dependent field, which is a field whose value can differ between companies, so the web theme can highlight it. It also adds a phone field on contacts as part of its model changes.

name: company_sanitary_registry
summary: This module records a sanitary registry number (a health or regulatory registration) for each company, and links registries to warehouses and product categories. It also provides a template that can be printed on reports. It is set up on the company form and in warehouse and inventory settings.

name: company_sanitary_registry
summary: This module records a sanitary registry number (a health or regulatory registration) for each company, and links registries to warehouses and product categories. It also provides a template that can be printed on reports. It is set up on the company form and in warehouse and inventory settings.

name: component
summary: This is a technical base module for developers. It provides a component system, a way to register small reusable pieces of logic as an alternative to extending model classes, and it is the foundation of the Connector framework for integrating with other systems. It has no screens for end users.

name: component
summary: This is a technical base module from the OCA Connector project. It gives developers a component system, a way to register small reusable pieces of code and pick them by usage and backend instead of only through Python class inheritance. End users do not see anything in the interface; other connector modules build on it.

name: component_event
summary: This is a technical developer module that adds an event system (observer pattern) on top of the component module. Developers can fire events such as a record being created and let other code listen for them, without changing core Odoo code. Nothing new appears on screen for end users.

name: component_event
summary: This is a technical developer module that adds an event system (observer pattern) on top of the component module. Developers can fire events such as a record being created and let other code listen for them, without changing core Odoo code. Nothing new appears on screen for end users.

name: confirmation_wizard
summary: This is a helper module that lets developers show a confirmation pop-up during any action in Odoo. The user sees a message with Confirm and Cancel, and depending on how the developer set it up, confirming either runs a chosen method or simply closes the pop-up. It does nothing on its own until another module calls it.

name: connector
summary: This is a technical framework from the OCA Connector project for building integrations between Odoo and outside systems such as e-commerce platforms. It provides backend records that describe each external system, a job queue for sync tasks, and a binding model that links external IDs to Odoo records. It does nothing visible by itself and is the foundation for connector modules such as the Magento or PrestaShop connectors.

name: connector
summary: This is a technical framework from the OCA Connector project for building integrations between Odoo and outside systems such as e-commerce platforms. It provides backend records that describe each external system, a job queue for sync tasks, and a binding model that links external IDs to Odoo records. It does nothing visible by itself and is the foundation for connector modules such as the Magento or PrestaShop connectors.

name: connector_base_product
summary: This is a small bridge module that adds a Connector tab to the product form. The tab is where connector information for a product is shown, so users working with products can see the link to the external system. It is only useful when a connector module is installed.

name: connector_ecommerce
summary: This is a hidden technical layer shared by the e-commerce connectors such as Magento and PrestaShop. It adds sales order fields for cancellations from the online store, parent order links, and a tax group on products, plus payment mode import rules and a set of events that connectors can listen to. Users see the new fields on sales orders, payment modes, products, and deliveries.

name: connector_elasticsearch
summary: This module adds Elasticsearch as a search engine option for the search engine connector. Search engine backends get settings for the Elasticsearch host, SSL, API key or username and password login, timeouts, and retries. Records are then sent to Elasticsearch indexes from the Search Engine configuration screens.

name: connector_elasticsearch
summary: This module adds Elasticsearch as a search engine option for the search engine connector. Search engine backends get settings for the Elasticsearch host, SSL, API key or username and password login, timeouts, and retries. Records are then sent to Elasticsearch indexes from the Search Engine configuration screens.

name: connector_importer
summary: This module imports or updates Odoo records from files, with the work run through the job queue so large files do not block the screen. Setup is done in import backends, record sets, sources (CSV files), and import types that define which models to import and how. It can also run imports on a schedule and produce a summary report.

name: connector_importer
summary: This module imports or updates Odoo records from files, with the work run through the job queue so large files do not block the screen. Setup is done in import backends, record sets, sources (CSV files), and import types that define which models to import and how. It can also run imports on a schedule and produce a summary report.

name: connector_importer
summary: This module imports or updates Odoo records from files, with the work run through the job queue so large files do not block the screen. Setup is done in import backends, record sets, sources (CSV files), and import types that define which models to import and how. It can also run imports on a schedule and produce a summary report.

name: connector_importer_product
summary: This module provides ready-made import definitions for products on top of connector_importer. It covers products, product attributes and attribute values, product categories, packaging, and supplier information, so users can load these from files without building the import setup from scratch.

name: connector_importer_product
summary: This module provides ready-made import definitions for products on top of connector_importer. It covers products, product attributes and attribute values, product categories, packaging, and supplier information, so users can load these from files without building the import setup from scratch.

name: connector_importer_source_sftp
summary: This module adds an SFTP import source to connector_importer. CSV files placed in an input folder on an SFTP server are picked up and imported, then moved to a success or error folder depending on the result. Setup covers the folder paths, a filename pattern, and an option to send back an error report.

name: connector_jira
summary: This module syncs Jira Cloud with Odoo projects, tasks, and timesheets. Jira tasks and worklogs are imported into Odoo in one direction only, and Odoo projects can be created and exported to Jira. Jira links appear on projects, tasks, and timesheet lines in the Project and Timesheet apps, and the Jira backend holds the connection settings.

name: connector_jira_servicedesk
summary: This module extends the Jira connector for Jira Service Desk. It imports Jira organizations and lets each one be mapped to a different Odoo project, so work for different customer organizations lands in the right place. It also adds a service desk issue link to timesheet lines.

name: connector_search_engine
summary: This is a technical base module for sending Odoo records to external search engines such as Elasticsearch or Typesense. It defines the engine connection (backend), the indexes that say which model and fields to index, and per-record bindings that track sync state and errors. Users find it under the Search Engine configuration menus, and each indexed record shows counts of done, pending, and failed syncs.

name: connector_search_engine
summary: This is a technical base module for sending Odoo records to external search engines such as Elasticsearch or Typesense. It defines the engine connection (backend), the indexes that say which model and fields to index, and per-record bindings that track sync state and errors. Users find it under the Search Engine configuration menus, and each indexed record shows counts of done, pending, and failed syncs.

name: connector_search_engine_serializer_ir_export
summary: This module lets a search index use an existing export template (ir.exports) to decide which fields are sent to the search engine. Instead of writing code for the data format, an index can be pointed at an exporter. It extends the search index settings.

name: connector_typesense
summary: This module connects Odoo to a Typesense search server. It adds host, port, protocol, timeout, and API key settings to search engine backends, so records can be indexed in Typesense. The settings are found under Search Engine, Configuration, Backends.

name: connector_typesense
summary: This module connects Odoo to a Typesense search server. It adds host, port, protocol, timeout, and API key settings to search engine backends, so records can be indexed in Typesense. The settings are found under Search Engine, Configuration, Backends.

name: contract
summary: Manages recurring contracts for customers and suppliers, which generate invoices automatically on a schedule. Customer contracts are under Invoicing > Customers > Customer Contracts and supplier contracts under Invoicing > Vendors > Supplier Contracts, each with a journal, recurrence settings and contract lines. Portal users who follow a contract can see it, and the contract report can be printed or emailed.

name: contract
summary: This module manages recurring contracts with customers and suppliers, and creates the invoices automatically on a set interval. Contracts have a journal, a price list, lines for products with quantities and prices, and recurrence settings, and they can be found under Invoicing, Customers, Customer Contracts and Invoicing, Vendors, Supplier Contracts. Contracts can be printed or emailed, shown to followers on the portal, and handled with renewals, termination reasons, templates, and a modification log.

name: contract_analytic_tag
summary: This module adds analytic tags to recurring contract lines, so the invoices generated from those lines carry the same tags. This keeps cost and reporting tags consistent from the contract through to the invoice. The field appears on the contract lines.

name: contract_analytic_tag
summary: Lets you add analytic tags to contract lines, so the invoice lines generated from them carry those tags. This restores analytic tagging for recurring billing. It is set on each contract line.

name: contract_brand
summary: This module adds a Brand field to contracts and passes that brand on to the invoices created from them. It depends on the account and analytic brand modules, so brands must be set up there first. The brand appears on the contract form and the generated invoices.

name: contract_brand
summary: This module adds a Brand field to contracts and passes that brand on to the invoices created from them. It depends on the account and analytic brand modules, so brands must be set up there first. The brand appears on the contract form and the generated invoices.

name: contract_delivery_zone
summary: This module shows the partner's delivery zone on the contract itself, so anyone working on a contract can see which delivery zone applies. It adds a delivery zone field to contracts, taken from the customer's partner record.

name: contract_forecast
summary: Generates future forecast periods for each contract line, showing the expected invoice dates and amounts for the coming months or years. Forecasts open from the contract's Forecast button, in pivot or list view, and regenerate automatically when quantity, price or dates change. The number of periods and the monthly or yearly type are set in General Settings.

name: contract_forecast
summary: Technical analysis module that projects future contract billing. Each contract line gets forecast periods (date range, quantity, unit price, invoice date) so you can see what recurring invoices are expected going forward. Forecast periods are linked to contract lines, and the number of periods and the rule type are set per company in the Settings screen.

name: contract_forecast_brand
summary: Technical bridge module that carries the brand from contracts into contract forecasts, so forecast data can be viewed by brand. It adds no fields of its own and only has an effect when the contract brand module is also installed.

name: contract_forecast_variable_quantity
summary: Regenerates contract forecasts automatically when a contract line's quantity type or quantity formula changes. It joins the forecast and variable quantity features, so forecast figures stay in step with variable quantities. It is an integration add-on with no new screens.

name: contract_invoice_auto_validate
summary: Validates contract invoices automatically right after they are created, instead of leaving them as drafts. It is turned on with the Auto validate contract invoices company setting. The CONTRACT_INVOICE queue channel must have a capacity of 1 in the Odoo configuration to avoid sequence conflicts.

name: contract_invoice_manually
summary: Adds a Manually Invoiced option on contracts, which excludes them from automatic invoicing. They are then invoiced by hand from the Manually Invoice Sale Contracts or Manually Invoice Purchase Contracts menus, using a chosen date and filter. Manual invoicing must be enabled in the settings first.

name: contract_invoice_start_end_dates
summary: Adds start and end dates to the invoice lines generated from a contract, when the product is marked as Must have dates. The dates come from the contract line, so the invoice shows the service period. It is useful for subscriptions and other recurring services.

name: contract_layout_category_hide_detail
summary: Brings the section hide-detail options to contracts, so each section can hide its line details, its subtotal or its line amounts. These choices carry into the contract report, the customer portal and the invoices generated from the contract. Section settings from a sales order are passed on to the contract.

name: contract_line_successor
summary: Manages the life of each contract line, including stopping, suspending, cancelling, renewing and planning a successor line. Lines carry states such as In-Progress, To Renew and Closed, and auto-renewal can either extend a line or create a new one. Turn on Recurrence at line level in the contract, then use the line actions.

name: contract_mandate
summary: Lets a contract carry a direct debit mandate, so the recurring invoices it creates are tied to that mandate. You pick the mandate on the contract form, can mark it as required, and the mandate is carried onto each generated invoice. It is found on the Contracts screen under Sales.

name: contract_mandate
summary: Lets you choose a direct debit mandate on a contract, so the invoices it generates use that mandate. Select the partner, the mandate and the recurrence, and each new invoice carries the mandate. It is set on the contract form.

name: contract_membership_delegated_partner
summary: Lets you set a delegated membership member on a contract, so the recurring invoices it creates automatically name that delegated partner. You choose the delegate on the contract form. Users need the Delegated partner in membership permission to use it.

name: contract_membership_delegated_partner
summary: Lets you set a delegated membership member on a contract, so the recurring invoices it creates automatically name that delegated partner. You choose the delegate on the contract form. Users need the Delegated partner in membership permission to use it.

name: contract_operating_unit
summary: Adds an Operating Unit field to contracts so each contract can be assigned to a specific operating unit within a company. Security rules then limit users to contracts from the operating units they have access to. You set it on the contract form in the Contracts screen.

name: contract_operating_unit
summary: Adds an Operating Unit field to contracts so each contract can be assigned to a specific operating unit within a company. Security rules then limit users to contracts from the operating units they have access to. You set it on the contract form in the Contracts screen.

name: contract_operating_unit_access_all
summary: Adds a user setting that lets one user see contracts from all operating units without being added to each one. It is a checkbox on the user record under Settings, Users and Companies. Use it for users who need company-wide visibility of contracts.

name: contract_payment_auto
summary: Lets recurring contract invoices be paid automatically using a saved payment token. You turn on Auto Pay on a contract, choose its payment token, and set the invoice, payment retry and payment failed email templates along with how many retries to attempt and how many hours apart. Invoices record their auto pay attempts and failures, and the setting is also available on contract templates.

name: contract_payment_mode
summary: Lets a contract store a payment mode, so the recurring invoices it creates use that payment method. The partner's default payment mode is pre-filled, and you can change it on the contract form. Users need to be a Sales Manager or Accountant to set it.

name: contract_payment_mode
summary: Lets you choose a payment mode on a contract, so its invoices use that payment mode. The contract starts with the customer's payment mode and it can be changed. It is set on the contract form under Invoicing > Customers > Customer Contracts.

name: contract_payment_mode_brand
summary: Limits the payment mode choices on a contract to the ones allowed for the contract's brand. Allowed payment modes are set per brand under Settings, Users and Companies, Brands. When you pick a brand on a new contract, the payment mode list only shows what that brand allows.

name: contract_price_revision
summary: Lets you raise or set contract line prices in bulk from a wizard, either by a percentage or to a fixed price, from a chosen start date. Select the contracts, run Create revision of contract lines from the Action menu, and set the date range and the change. Previous prices are kept on each line for reference.

name: contract_queue_job
summary: Technical setting for large contract billing runs. Instead of creating every recurring invoice in one long transaction, the nightly contract invoicing cron queues one background job per contract, so one failure does not stop the others. It is switched on with a system parameter named contract.queue.job.

name: contract_queue_job
summary: Makes the contract invoicing cron job create one background job per contract, rather than creating all invoices in a single transaction. This means one failure does not hold up every other invoice. It is enabled with the contract.queue.job system parameter.

name: contract_refund_on_stop
summary: Lets you stop a contract line after it has been invoiced. If the stop date is earlier than the last invoiced date, a refund invoice is created for the unused period and the line ends on the stop date. It needs the prorated variable quantity module, and it is enabled under Invoicing > Configuration > Settings in the Contracts section.

name: contract_sale
summary: Gives sales users access to contracts without accounting rights. Users in the sales Only Own Documents group see only the contracts they created, and can open them under Sales > Sales > Contracts. This lets sales staff manage recurring contracts without billing access.

name: contract_sale
summary: Lets sales staff who do not have accounting rights open and manage contracts from Sales > Sales > Contracts. Users in the sales group with the Only Own Documents right see only the contracts they created. It does not add new fields; it changes who can access the contracts screen.

name: contract_sale_generation
summary: Lets a contract generate sales orders instead of invoices. Set the contract Type to Sales, and optionally have the sales orders it creates confirmed automatically. This is useful when recurring work needs an order before it is invoiced.

name: contract_sale_generation
summary: Lets a recurring contract create sales orders instead of invoices. On the contract you choose the generation type (Sales or Invoices), and can turn on Sale Autoconfirm so generated sales orders are confirmed automatically. Generated sales orders link back to their contract, and the contract shows a count of them.

name: contract_sale_invoicing
summary: Adds pending sales orders that share an analytic account to the recurring invoice a contract generates, so they are billed together. Tick Invoice Pending Sales Orders on the contract. Each invoicing run checks for unbilled orders on that analytic account.

name: contract_sale_invoicing_pricelist
summary: Makes recurring invoices created from a contract use the contract's pricelist and currency. Without it, generated invoices fall back to the customer's default pricing. It has no new fields of its own; it changes how the recurring invoices are priced.

name: contract_sale_mandate
summary: Carries the direct debit mandate from a sales order to the contract it creates, and from there to the contract's invoices. It joins the sales mandate, contract mandate and product contract features together. It adds no new screens of its own.

name: contract_sale_payment_mode
summary: Carries the payment mode from a sales order to the contract it creates. A company setting allows a separate payment mode for contracts created from sales orders, which is set on the order. The contract's invoices then use that payment mode.

name: contract_sale_transmit_method
summary: Carries the transmit method (email, post or portal) from a sales order to the contract it creates, so the contract's invoices are sent the same way. It joins the sales transmit method, contract transmit method and product contract features. It adds no new screens of its own.

name: contract_service_dates
summary: Adds separate Service Start Date and Service End Date fields to contract lines, so the actual service period can differ from the billing dates. The dates fill in from the line start and end dates automatically but can be overridden by hand. They appear in a Service Dates group on the Recurrence tab of a contract line.

name: contract_termination
summary: Lets users terminate a contract with a reason, comment and date using a Terminate Contract button. Once terminated, the contract becomes read-only and shows an alert with the termination details, and the termination can be updated or cancelled to reactivate the contract. Termination reasons are set up under Contracts configuration, and only users with the Can Terminate Contracts right can do this.

name: contract_transmit_method
summary: Adds a transmission method, such as email, post or portal, to contracts and contract templates. The chosen method is carried over to the invoices created from the contract, so invoices go out the way the customer expects. The field appears on the contract form.

name: contract_update_last_date_invoiced
summary: Lets you reset a contract line's last invoiced date and next recurring date after invoices have been deleted, so the recurring billing picks up again from the right date. Open a contract and click Update Last Date Invoiced, then enter the date you want. It is found under Invoicing, Customers, Customer Contracts.

name: contract_update_last_date_invoiced
summary: Adds a wizard to reset the last invoiced date on a contract line, for example after invoices were deleted, so the next recurring invoice is generated from the correct date. It is opened from the customer contracts list and also lets you set the next invoice date.

name: contract_variable_qty_prorated
summary: Adds a prorated quantity formula for contract lines with a variable quantity, so a partial billing period is invoiced in proportion to the days covered. It only adds the formula; the variable quantity setup itself comes from the contract variable quantity module. It is used on recurring contract invoicing lines.

name: contract_variable_qty_timesheet
summary: Lets a recurring contract line be invoiced from the hours recorded on timesheets, using project timesheets, task timesheets or analytic lines. You pick one of the timesheet quantity types on a recurring invoicing line, and the invoiced quantity comes from the logged time. It is set up on the Contracts recurring invoicing lines.

name: contract_variable_qty_timesheet
summary: Lets recurring contract lines bill based on time recorded on timesheets. When a line's quantity type is Variable quantity, you can choose Project Timesheets, Tasks Timesheets or Analytic Same Product as the source, so the invoiced quantity comes from logged hours. It is set on the recurring invoicing lines under Invoicing, Customers, Customer Contracts.

name: contract_variable_quantity
summary: Lets recurring contract lines have a quantity that changes with each invoice, calculated by a formula the admin defines once under Contracts configuration, Formulas. Choosing the Variable quantity type on a recurring line makes the formula set how much is invoiced. Contracts can also be set to skip lines whose computed quantity is zero.

name: cooperator
summary: Full cooperative membership module. It manages subscription requests for shares, capital release invoices, share types, transfers and departures of cooperators, and a Cooperator Registry, with reports and certificates. Shares show on the partner form, and a localization module is required alongside it.

name: cooperator_documentation
summary: Small technical add-on that puts a link to the Cooperator module documentation in the menu bar. It has no business logic of its own.

name: cooperator_portal
summary: Lets cooperators log in to the website portal to see their cooperator information and access their personal documents and certificates. On the My Account page, name and email are locked and IBAN, birth date, gender and language become required. The security page's account deletion button is disabled.

name: cooperator_website
summary: Adds an online subscription form to the website so people can apply for cooperative shares without contacting staff. Submitted requests appear in the cooperator subscription workflow. It needs the Cooperator and Website modules.

name: cooperator_website_payment
summary: Lets people pay for their cooperative shares online during the website subscription process. It connects the subscription request to website payments and records the payment transaction against the request and its invoice.

name: cooperator_website_recaptcha
summary: Adds Google reCAPTCHA to the online cooperator subscription form to block bots and automated sign-ups. It only applies to the website form.

name: coupon_chatter
summary: Adds the chatter to loyalty programs, so users can log notes, send messages and schedule activities on discount, loyalty, gift card and eWallet programs. Open a program under Sales, Products, Discount and Loyalty (or Gift cards and eWallet) to see the chatter at the bottom of the form.

name: coupon_chatter
summary: Adds the chatter, so messages and activities can be logged and scheduled on sale coupon and gift card programs. Open a program under Sales > Products > Discount & Loyalty or Gift cards & eWallet to see the chatter panel.

name: crm_claim
summary: Lets you record customer or supplier claims and complaints as tracked records, with categories, stages, deadlines and a resolution field. Claims live under CRM > After Sale > Services > Claims, and new claims can be created automatically from incoming emails. Partners also get a claim count and a list of their claims.

name: crm_claim_analytic
summary: Links a claim to an analytic account so the costs and revenue tied to a claim can be tracked. The claim form gets an analytic account and amount field, and analytic lines can point back to the claim. Users need the Analytic Accounting group, and it depends on the claims module.

name: crm_claim_code
summary: Gives every claim a sequential Claim Number when it is saved. The number shows on the claim form under CRM > After Sale > Claims.

name: crm_claim_code
summary: Gives every claim a sequential Claim Number when it is saved. The number shows on the claim form under CRM > After Sale > Claims.

name: crm_claim_type
summary: Lets you classify claims as Customer, Supplier or Other, and set different stages depending on the claim type. Claim types are managed under CRM > Configuration > Claim > Claim Types, and each claim gets a Claim Type field.

name: crm_claim_type
summary: Lets you classify claims as Customer, Supplier or Other, and set different stages depending on the claim type. Claim types are managed under CRM > Configuration > Claim > Claim Types, and each claim gets a Claim Type field.

name: crm_date_deadline_required
summary: Makes the Expected Closing date a required field on CRM opportunities, so an opportunity cannot be saved until a closing date is filled in. Users see an error on save if it is left empty.

name: crm_event
summary: Links CRM leads and opportunities to an event type, so you can see how many leads want each kind of event. On an event template, an Events smart button counts upcoming or running events and the seats wanted by opportunities. Includes an event type analysis report.

name: crm_event
summary: Links CRM leads and opportunities to an event category, so you can see how many leads want each category of event. On an event template, an Events smart button counts upcoming or running events and the seats wanted by opportunities. Includes an event categories analysis report.

name: crm_exception
summary: Lets you attach configurable exception rules to CRM opportunities, limited to chosen pipeline stages. Rules are defined with the base exception framework under the exception rules menu, and matching opportunities are flagged with the exception.

name: crm_exception
summary: Lets you attach configurable exception rules to CRM opportunities, limited to chosen pipeline stages. Rules are defined with the base exception framework under the exception rules menu, and matching opportunities are flagged with the exception.

name: crm_industry
summary: Adds a main industry and a list of secondary industries to leads and opportunities, so the pipeline can be grouped by sector. The fields appear on the lead or opportunity form under CRM.

name: crm_lead_code
summary: Gives every lead or opportunity a sequential Lead Number when it is created. The number shows on the lead or opportunity form under CRM.

name: crm_lead_currency
summary: Lets a lead or opportunity have its own customer currency and an amount in that currency. When the currency differs from the company currency, the expected revenue is computed in company currency using the rate of the day. Multi-currency must be enabled for it to be useful.

name: crm_lead_currency
summary: Lets a lead or opportunity have its own customer currency and an amount in that currency. When the currency differs from the company currency, the expected revenue is computed in company currency using the rate of the day. Multi-currency must be enabled for it to be useful.

name: crm_lead_firstname
summary: Splits the contact name on leads into First name and Last name fields, and carries them over to the customer when a lead is converted. The fields appear on the lead form and on the opportunity Followup tab.

name: crm_lead_firstname
summary: Splits the contact name on leads into First name and Last name fields, and carries them over to the customer when a lead is converted. The fields appear on the lead form and on the opportunity Followup tab.

name: crm_lead_product
summary: Lets you add several products, product categories or product templates to a lead or opportunity, with expected and prorated revenue per line. A pivot and graph report under CRM > Reporting > Pipeline by Product shows revenue by product and stage, for product demand forecasting.

name: crm_lead_product
summary: Lets you add several products, product categories or product templates to a lead or opportunity, with planned and expected revenue per line. A pivot and graph report under CRM > Reporting > Pipeline by Product shows revenue by product and stage, for product demand forecasting.

name: crm_lead_search_archive
summary: Adds a search filter on CRM leads that also includes archived records, so an archived lead can be found from the search bar. It only changes what the search finds, not the archive itself.

name: crm_lead_to_task
summary: Turns a lead or opportunity into a project task, bringing along its attachments and messages. A Convert to Task button on the lead form opens a popup to pick a project, or a forced project can be set in CRM settings. Settings can also archive the lead after conversion.

name: crm_lead_to_task
summary: Lets you convert a lead or opportunity into a project task using a Convert to Task button on the lead form. A popup asks for the project, and the new task keeps the lead's information, attachments and messages.

name: crm_lead_to_task
summary: Lets you convert a lead or opportunity into a project task using a Convert to Task button on the lead form. A popup asks for the project, and the new task keeps the lead's information, attachments and messages.

name: crm_lead_vat
summary: Adds a VAT (tax ID) field to CRM leads that stays in sync with the contact's VAT. If the VAT is changed on the lead, a warning says that saving will update the partner. The field is on the lead form under CRM > Leads.

name: crm_lead_vat
summary: Adds a VAT (tax ID) field to CRM leads that stays in sync with the contact's VAT. If the VAT is changed on the lead, a warning says that saving will update the partner. The field is on the lead form under CRM > Leads.

name: crm_location
summary: Improves address entry on leads: zip, city, state and country auto-complete from the zip code. Works on the lead form under CRM.

name: crm_location_nuts
summary: Adds EU NUTS region fields (levels 1 to 4) to leads and opportunities, and copies them to the customer when the opportunity is converted. Set them on the lead form under CRM.

name: crm_lost_reason_multi_company
summary: Gives lost reasons a company field, so each company in a multi-company database can keep its own list of reasons an opportunity was lost. Technical, mainly relevant to multi-company setups.

name: crm_lost_reason_multi_company
summary: Gives lost reasons a company field, so each company in a multi-company database can keep its own list of reasons an opportunity was lost. Technical, mainly relevant to multi-company setups.

name: crm_lost_reason_required
summary: Makes the lost reason required when a lead or opportunity is marked as lost, going by the module title. Its own description is an unfilled template, so this is inferred from the name only.

name: crm_lost_reason_required
summary: Makes the Lost Reason mandatory in the Mark as Lost wizard, so a lead or opportunity cannot be marked lost until a reason is picked. Standard Odoo leaves this optional. No configuration is needed.

name: crm_membership
summary: Shows membership status, start date and end date on CRM leads and opportunities. Use it to see whether a prospect is already a member, from the membership module.

name: crm_operating_unit
summary: Adds an Operating Unit to leads and opportunities, filled in from the user's default sales team or default operating unit. Users only see leads in operating units they can access, and can filter by operating unit. Found on the lead form and in CRM filters.

name: crm_partner_assign
summary: Lets you assign an associate partner, such as a reseller or implementation partner, to a lead, plus a specific partner contact, so you can see which leads a partner is working on. Partners can also be linked to another partner as their implementation partner, shown on the partner form.

name: crm_partner_assign
summary: Lets you assign an associate partner, such as a reseller or implementation partner, to a lead, plus a specific partner contact, so you can see which leads a partner is working on. Partners can also be linked to another partner as their implementation partner, shown on the partner form.

name: crm_partner_capital
summary: Adds capital, turnover range and company size fields to leads, taken from the partner capital data. They are filled in on the lead's Additional Information tab and saved to the company contact when the lead is converted.

name: crm_partner_company_group
summary: Adds a Company Group field to leads and opportunities in CRM, so pipeline records can be grouped by the customer's company group. It requires the base company group module.

name: crm_partner_company_group
summary: Adds a Company Group field to leads, so a lead can be tied to a group of related companies. The group itself is defined in the base company group module.

name: crm_partner_employee_quantity
summary: Adds an employee count and an employee count range to leads and opportunities. They are filled in on the lead's Additional Information tab and saved to the company contact on conversion.

name: crm_partner_required
summary: Makes the Customer field required on CRM opportunities, so an opportunity cannot be saved without a customer. Users get an error on save if it is left empty.

name: crm_phonecall
summary: Lets you log phone calls against contacts and opportunities, categorise them, schedule the next call or meeting, and convert a call into an opportunity. Calls are under CRM > Phone Calls, and can be analysed by user and team.

name: crm_phonecall_planner
summary: Builds a phone call schedule for partners based on their preferred calling times. Use the Planner under CRM > Phone Calls to generate calls from chosen criteria, after setting each partner's preferred calling schedule on their form.

name: crm_phonecall_result
summary: Adds a Result field to phone calls, with a list of result options you define under CRM > Configuration > Calls. Calls can be filtered and grouped by result, and the result also appears in the phone call report.

name: crm_phonecall_summary_predefined
summary: Lets sales managers define a fixed list of phone call summaries, so users pick one from a Summary field on a logged call instead of typing freely. The list is set under CRM > Configuration > Phone Calls > Summaries.

name: crm_project_create
summary: Creates a project from a lead or opportunity with a Create project button in the header, using a wizard for the project name and description. The project can also be archived or reactivated from the lead, and is linked from the lead's Extra Information tab.

name: crm_project_create
summary: Creates a project from a lead or opportunity with a Create project button in the header, using a wizard for the project name and description. The project can also be archived or reactivated from the lead, and is linked from the lead form.

name: crm_project_task
summary: Lets salespeople create tasks linked to a lead or opportunity, in a default CRM project set in CRM settings. A Create Task button on the lead opens a wizard or the task form, and the task links back to the lead.

name: crm_project_task
summary: Lets salespeople create a task from a lead or opportunity with a Create Task button, using the default CRM project from settings. The task gets a chatter message linking back to the lead.

name: crm_salesperson_planner
summary: Lets you schedule and track salesperson visits to customers. Each visit creates an all-day calendar event, visits can be generated from recurring templates by a scheduled job, and each visit lists the opportunities to discuss. Found under CRM > Salesperson Planner.

name: crm_salesperson_planner
summary: Lets you schedule and track salesperson visits to customers. Each visit creates an all-day calendar event, visits can be generated from recurring templates by a scheduled job, and each visit lists the opportunities to discuss. Found under CRM > Salesperson Planner.

name: crm_salesperson_planner
summary: Lets you schedule and track salesperson visits to customers. Each visit creates an all-day calendar event, visits can be generated from recurring templates by a scheduled job, and each visit lists the opportunities to discuss. Found under CRM > Salesperson Planner.

name: crm_salesperson_planner_sale
summary: Lets you create a sales quotation from a validated or visited salesperson visit, using a New Quotation button or smart button on the visit. The quotation and sale order link back to the visit.

name: crm_security_group
summary: Adds four CRM access levels (Own Documents Only, Team Documents Only, All Documents and Administrator), so CRM users can be limited without giving them full Sales access. Assigned through user access rights.

name: crm_security_group
summary: Adds four CRM access levels (Own Documents Only, Team Documents Only, All Documents and Administrator), so CRM users can be limited without giving them full Sales access. Assigned through user access rights.

name: crm_sign_oca
summary: Lets you send a document for e-signature from a CRM lead, using a sign template you configure. Signed documents are linked back to the lead. Open the lead, click the gear button and choose Sign from template.

name: crm_stage_mail
summary: Sends an email automatically when a lead moves into a pipeline stage, using an email template set on that stage. For example, a welcome email goes out when a lead reaches Qualified.

name: crm_stage_mail
summary: Sends an email automatically when a lead moves into a pipeline stage, using an email template set on that stage. For example, a welcome email goes out when a lead reaches Qualified.

name: crm_stage_multi_company
summary: Lets CRM pipeline stages belong to a specific company, so each company sees its own stages. Users who lack access to all stages can still open the CRM app.

name: crm_stage_multi_company
summary: Lets CRM pipeline stages belong to a specific company, so each company sees its own stages. Users who lack access to all stages can still open the CRM app.

name: crm_stage_multi_team
summary: Lets a pipeline stage be shared by several sales teams, while other stages stay exclusive to one team. Each team's kanban shows only its relevant stages, and stages with no team show for everyone. Set teams on each stage under CRM > Configuration > Stages.

name: crm_stage_multi_team
summary: Lets a pipeline stage be shared by several sales teams, while other stages stay exclusive to one team. Each team's kanban shows only its relevant stages, and stages with no team show for everyone. Set teams on each stage under CRM > Configuration > Stages.

name: crm_stage_probability
summary: Sets a fixed win probability on each pipeline stage, restoring the Odoo 12 behaviour where a lead's probability follows its stage. An Update leads probability wizard on the stages applies the new probabilities to existing leads. Stage probabilities are set under CRM > Configuration > Stages.

name: crm_stage_probability
summary: Sets a fixed win probability on each pipeline stage, restoring the Odoo 12 behaviour where a lead's probability follows its stage. An Update leads probability wizard on the stages applies the new probabilities to existing leads. Stage probabilities are set under CRM > Configuration > Stages.

name: crm_tag_multi_company
summary: Gives CRM tags a company field, so each company keeps its own tags on leads and opportunities. Technical change for multi-company databases.

name: crm_tag_multi_company_event_crm
summary: Makes the tag check in event lead rules respect the company, so tags from another company cannot be used there. Technical, for multi-company databases that use event lead rules.

name: crm_tag_multi_company_sale
summary: Makes the tag check on sale orders respect the company, so only tags from the current company can be put on a quotation. Technical, for multi-company setups.

name: crm_team_parent
summary: Adds a Parent Team field to sales teams so they can be arranged in a hierarchy, and blocks loops in that hierarchy. The field appears on the sales team form and list under CRM > Configuration > Sales Teams.

name: crm_team_zip_assign
summary: Automatically assigns a sales team to a partner based on the partner's ZIP code, matching regular expression patterns set per team and filtered by country and state. Teams have a priority, and partners can be excluded. Set up on each sales team's ZIP Patterns tab, and runs when partner address data changes or from a manual action on partner views.

name: crm_timesheet
summary: Lets you record timesheet time directly on CRM leads and opportunities, with a Timesheet tab on the lead form. It also links a lead to a project. It appears on the lead form in the CRM app.

name: crm_won_reason
summary: Adds a Won Reason field to leads, picked in a wizard when an opportunity is marked as won. Lost reasons also get a type selection. It extends the lead win and loss flow in the CRM app.

name: crm_won_restrict_per_stage
summary: Lets you choose which pipeline stages show the Won button. Where a stage has it unchecked, the button is hidden and leads there cannot be moved straight into a won stage. Set under CRM > Configuration > Pipelines > Stages; every existing stage shows the button after install.

name: crm_won_restrict_per_stage
summary: Lets you choose which pipeline stages show the Won button. Where a stage has it unchecked, the button is hidden and leads there cannot be moved straight into a won stage. Set under CRM > Configuration > Pipelines > Stages; every existing stage shows the button after install.

name: cron_daylight_saving_time_resistant
summary: Keeps scheduled actions running at the same local clock time across daylight saving changes. Tick Daylight Saving Time Resistant on a scheduled action under Settings > Technical > Automation > Scheduled Actions. Technical.

name: cross_connect_client
summary: Lets users of this Odoo instance sign in to another Odoo instance that has the cross connect server module installed. The other server is configured under Technical settings with its URL and API key. It is a technical integration.

name: cross_connect_server
summary: Lets other Odoo instances log their users into this one, through a FastAPI endpoint with an allowed group list and client API keys. Clients are set up under the FastAPI endpoints menu. It is the server side of a technical integration.

name: crowdfunding
summary: Turns Odoo into a crowdfunding platform. Backend users create challenges with a target amount and commission fee, and vendor bills pay out the funds. Backers see the challenges on the website at /crowdfunding, where they can join the discussion and pledge.

name: crowdfunding_demo
summary: Demo setup for crowdfunding that creates and configures payment providers so the feature can be tried on a test instance. Technical, meant for test databases rather than live use.

name: crowdfunding_public_pledge
summary: Lets a logged-in backer mark a pledge as public on the website, so it appears under the challenge description once paid. Backend users can also flag pledges as public from the crowdfunding tab of an invoice.

name: crowdfunding_schedule
summary: Adds start and end date and time to crowdfunding challenges, so pledges are accepted only inside that window. The website shows countdowns and status messages before, during and after the challenge.

name: currency_old_rate_notify
summary: Warns billing administrators when the latest exchange rate for a currency is older than a set number of days (3 by default), so converted amounts are not silently based on stale rates. The limit is set under Invoicing > Configuration > Settings in the Currencies section.

name: currency_old_rate_notify
summary: Warns billing administrators when the latest exchange rate for a currency is older than a set number of days (3 by default), so converted amounts are not silently based on stale rates. The limit is set under Invoicing > Configuration > Settings in the Currencies section.

name: currency_rate_update
summary: Pulls exchange rates automatically from providers, starting with the European Central Bank, either on a schedule or for a chosen date range through an Update Rates wizard. Providers are set up under Invoicing > Configuration > Currency Rates Providers, and automatic updates are enabled in the settings.

name: currency_rate_update
summary: Pulls exchange rates automatically from providers, starting with the European Central Bank, either on a schedule or for a chosen date range through an Update Rates wizard. Providers are set up under Invoicing > Configuration > Currency Rates Providers, and automatic updates are enabled in the settings.

name: currency_rate_update_xe
summary: Adds XE.com as a Source Service choice on a currency rates provider, so exchange rates can be pulled from XE.com. The rates are read from a public web page rather than an official API.

name: currency_rate_update_xe
summary: Adds XE.com as a Source Service choice on a currency rates provider, so exchange rates can be pulled from XE.com. The rates are read from a public web page rather than an official API.

name: data_encryption
summary: Technical base module that encrypts and decrypts stored data, with a separate key per environment such as dev, test or production. It has no screens of its own and is meant to be used by other modules to store credentials safely.

name: data_encryption
summary: Technical base module that encrypts and decrypts stored data, with a separate key per environment such as dev, test or production. It has no screens of its own and is meant to be used by other modules to store credentials safely.

name: database_autovacuum_tuning
summary: Shows administrators recommended PostgreSQL autovacuum thresholds for their database, with guidance on sizing them. Values can be overridden with system parameters, and the page is under Settings, Technical, Database Structure, Database Autovacuum Tuning. It is mainly useful for PostgreSQL 17 and older.

name: database_cleanup
summary: Technical maintenance tool that finds and removes leftovers from uninstalled modules, such as orphaned models, columns, tables, menus and attachments. It can damage data if misused. Under Settings > Technical > Database cleanup, only users in the Access Rights group can use it.

name: database_cleanup
summary: A risky administrator tool that finds leftover models, fields, tables, menus and data from uninstalled modules and lets the admin purge them. It is found under Settings, Technical, Database Cleanup and only Access Rights administrators can see it. Misuse can damage data, so it should only be used by experienced developers.

name: database_size
summary: Takes a daily snapshot of how much disk space the database and attachments use, and shows how the size of each model has changed over time. Reports are under Settings, Technical, Database, with an option to keep only a set number of older measurements. It helps admins watch growth and plan storage.

name: datamodel
summary: Technical base for defining simple data models that serialise to and from JSON, used by the REST framework. Developers write datamodel classes, and the module adds no screens for business users.

name: date_range
summary: Lets you define global date ranges, such as fiscal periods or quarters, and use them to filter list views. Range types and ranges are set up under Settings > Technical > Date ranges. Developers can also give their own models a period search field.

name: date_range
summary: Lets admins define named date periods such as fiscal years, quarters or months, and use them to filter list views. A wizard can generate recurring periods automatically. Date ranges and types are under Settings, Technical, Date Ranges, and any model can add a period search field to its search bar.

name: date_range_account
summary: Small glue module that puts the Date Range menu under Invoicing > Configuration, so accounting managers can manage date ranges from the accounting app. Only the menu access changes; the date ranges themselves come from the date range module.

name: date_range_account
summary: Adds the Date Range menu to the Invoicing app so accounting managers can reach it directly. It is a small link module between Date Range and Accounting. Accountants use it to set up their fiscal periods from the Invoicing configuration menu.

name: datetime_formatter
summary: Technical helper for developers that formats date, time and datetime values for display in the user's language and format. Business users should see no change from it; it is mostly pulled in as a dependency by other modules.

name: dbfilter_from_header
summary: Technical setting that lets a reverse proxy select the Odoo database through an HTTP header, for setups where database names cannot be mapped to host names. It is configured in the web server (nginx, Caddy or Apache), not in Odoo screens.

name: dbfilter_from_header
summary: Lets a web server choose which database to open by sending the database filter in an HTTP header. This is for hosting setups where database names cannot be matched to host names. It is an infrastructure setting with no effect on users.

name: ddmrp
summary: Implements Demand Driven Material Requirements Planning (DDMRP) in Odoo. Stock buffers are set per product and location, using buffer profiles with lead time and variability factors, and the module computes buffer zones, net flow position and procurement priorities. Buffers can launch purchase orders, manufacturing orders and transfer orders.

name: ddmrp
summary: Implements Demand Driven Material Requirements Planning (DDMRP) in Odoo. Stock buffers are set per product and location, using buffer profiles with lead time and variability factors, and the module computes buffer zones, net flow position and procurement priorities. Buffers can launch purchase orders, manufacturing orders and transfer orders.

name: ddmrp_adjustment
summary: Lets planners apply planned changes to stock buffers over a period: demand adjustments that change average daily usage, lead time adjustments, and zone adjustments for the red, yellow and green zones. Adjustments are managed under Inventory > Demand Planning > Buffer Adjustments.

name: ddmrp_adjustment
summary: Lets planners apply planned changes to stock buffers over a period: demand adjustments that change average daily usage, lead time adjustments, and zone adjustments for the red, yellow and green zones. Planning is done through a sheet opened from Inventory > Demand Planning > Create Buffer Adjustments.

name: ddmrp_adjustment_matrix
summary: Adds a 2D matrix wizard for entering DDMRP buffer adjustments in bulk, with periods and factors laid out as a grid, across many buffers at once. Opened from Inventory > Demand Planning > Create Buffer Adjustments.

name: ddmrp_chatter
summary: Adds a chatter with messages, notes and activities to stock buffers, so the planning team can discuss and track follow-ups on each buffer. The chatter appears on the stock buffer form.

name: ddmrp_coverage_days
summary: Shows how many days of stock coverage the current on-hand gives for each stock buffer, as a Days of Coverage field on the buffer. The figure appears on the stock buffer form.

name: ddmrp_cron_actions_as_job
summary: Runs DDMRP buffer calculations as background queue jobs instead of one large batch, so big buffer sets do not block the system. Each buffer is calculated as its own job, and duplicate jobs for the same buffer are merged. Technical, needs the queue job module.

name: ddmrp_cron_actions_as_job
summary: Runs DDMRP buffer calculations as background queue jobs instead of one large batch, so big buffer sets do not block the system. Each buffer is calculated as its own job, and duplicate jobs for the same buffer are merged. Technical, needs the queue job module.

name: ddmrp_exclude_moves_adu_calc
summary: Lets you exclude specific stock moves, or all moves into a chosen location, from the average daily usage calculation on buffers. Use the Exclude from ADU action on stock moves under Inventory > Reports > Stock Moves, or tick the flag on locations under Inventory > Configuration.

name: ddmrp_exclude_moves_adu_calc
summary: Lets you exclude specific stock moves, or all moves into a chosen location, from the average daily usage calculation on buffers. Use the Exclude from ADU action on stock moves under Inventory > Reports > Stock Moves, or tick the flag on locations under Inventory > Configuration.

name: ddmrp_exclude_moves_adu_calc_sales
summary: Adds an Exclude from ADU flag on sales order lines, so sales that should not count as normal demand can be left out of buffer average daily usage. Needs the Sales app and the ADU exclusion module.

name: ddmrp_exclude_moves_adu_calc_sales
summary: Adds an Exclude from ADU flag on sales order lines, so sales that should not count as normal demand can be left out of buffer average daily usage. Needs the Sales app and the ADU exclusion module.

name: ddmrp_history
summary: Stores a history of each DDMRP buffer's zones, net flow position, on-hand and average daily usage over time. Inventory managers see the full history under Inventory > Reports > DDMRP Buffer History, and a chart on each buffer form shows how it has moved.

name: ddmrp_include_location_final
summary: Technical fix that makes DDMRP use the final destination location logic from Odoo push rules, so buffers are computed against the right location on multi-step routes. The module notes this logic should move into the base DDMRP module later.

name: ddmrp_packaging
summary: Connects product packagings to stock buffers, so buffer quantities can be set in full packs and procurement lines can use a package quantity. Shows as Packaging fields on each buffer and on the buffer procurement wizard lines.

name: ddmrp_packaging_product_replace
summary: Technical glue between DDMRP packaging and product replacement. It stops the old product's packaging being copied onto the replacement buffer, which would otherwise fail a packaging check.

name: ddmrp_product_replace
summary: Adds a Product Replacement Tool under Inventory > Configuration > DDMRP. It either creates a new buffer for a replacement product or switches existing buffers over to it, and marks the replaced buffers.

name: ddmrp_purchase_hide_onhand_status
summary: Removes the On-Hand Status information from purchase order lines to speed up large purchase orders, and adds a smart button on each line to view it when needed. It only changes what the purchase order form displays.

name: ddmrp_report_part_flow_index
summary: Adds a Parts Plan Flow Index report under Inventory > Reporting. It groups buffers by a flow index group to show order frequency and green zone size. Groups are defined under Inventory > Configuration > DDMRP and assigned to each buffer.

name: ddmrp_sale
summary: Connects DDMRP buffers to the Sales app, so sales quotations count as incoming demand for buffers. A Can Serve Sales flag on each buffer decides which buffers treat quotations as demand.

name: ddmrp_sale_dropshipping
summary: Stops quotation demand from counting toward buffers for dropshipped products, by forcing the dropship route on the sale line. Needs the DDMRP Sale and dropshipping modules.

name: ddmrp_sale_order_line_date
summary: Makes DDMRP use the delivery date on each sale order line, instead of one delivery date for the whole order, when calculating buffer demand. Useful when lines on one order ship on different dates. Needs the sale order line date module.

name: ddmrp_warning
summary: Flags configuration problems on stock buffers using built-in warning rules and any you define. Filter buffers by Has Warnings, open the Warnings tab on a buffer to see active warnings, and use Refresh Warnings after fixing them.

name: ddmrp_warning
summary: Flags configuration problems on stock buffers using built-in warning rules and any you define. Filter buffers by Has Warnings, open the Warnings tab on a buffer to see active warnings, and use Refresh Warnings after fixing them.

name: ddmrp_warning_as_job
summary: Runs the DDMRP warning checks as background queue jobs, in the same way buffer calculations run, so large buffer sets are checked without blocking users. Technical, needs the queue job module.

name: default_multi_user
summary: Lets an admin share a user-defined default value, such as a default field setting for a form, with chosen users or groups. The sharing is set on the default record under Settings, Technical, Actions, User-defined Defaults. It saves each person from setting the same default themselves.

name: delivery_auto_refresh
summary: Keeps the shipping cost on draft sales orders up to date automatically. The delivery line recalculates when order lines change, can be added on save, and is adjusted when the delivered quantity differs from the ordered one. Options are under Settings > Sales > Shipping.

name: delivery_auto_refresh
summary: Keeps the shipping cost on draft sales orders up to date automatically. The delivery line recalculates when order lines change, can be added on save, and is adjusted when the delivered quantity differs from the ordered one. Options are under Settings > Sales > Shipping.

name: delivery_automatic_package
summary: Creates a package automatically when a delivery is validated, so tracking details can be recorded per package when the goods go to the carrier. It can be turned on for all shipping methods in Inventory settings, or per shipping method.

name: delivery_carrier_account
summary: Keeps carrier account records, with an account number and password, and links one to each shipping method, so the right account is used for a delivery. The Account field appears on the shipping method form.

name: delivery_carrier_account
summary: Keeps carrier account records, with an account number and password, and links one to each shipping method, so the right account is used for a delivery. The Account field appears on the shipping method form.

name: delivery_carrier_agency
summary: Adds carrier agencies, the offices or drop-off points a carrier uses. Each agency can be linked to shipping methods, a partner address and warehouses. The module stores the agencies only; any logic comes from carrier-specific modules.

name: delivery_carrier_agency
summary: Adds carrier agencies, the offices or drop-off points a carrier uses. Each agency can be linked to shipping methods, a partner address and warehouses. The module stores the agencies only; any logic comes from carrier-specific modules.

name: delivery_carrier_city
summary: Lets shipping methods use cities as a destination condition, using the city data from the address module. For example, a carrier can be offered only for certain cities. Set on the shipping method form.

name: delivery_carrier_deposit
summary: Groups outgoing deliveries by shipping method and date into a deposit slip, and prints a summary of all deliveries for each carrier, for handing over to the carrier. Created from the Warehouse menu with Create Deposit Slip.

name: delivery_carrier_global_manifest
summary: Prints one manifest file covering all carriers for a chosen date, and uses it as the default manifest when no carrier is picked. Carriers can be left out of the global manifest. Found under Inventory > Operations > Manifest.

name: delivery_carrier_image
summary: Lets you upload an image or logo for each shipping method, so the carrier's logo can be used in different screens and flows. Set it on the Delivery Carriers form under Inventory > Configuration > Delivery.

name: delivery_carrier_info
summary: Adds a Code field to shipping methods, for storing the carrier's own code or reference for that method. Fill it in on the shipping method form.

name: delivery_carrier_info
summary: Adds a Code field to shipping methods, for storing the carrier's own code or reference for that method. Fill it in on the shipping method form.

name: delivery_carrier_label_default
summary: Provides a basic shipping label to print when a delivery has no specific carrier selected. It is a technical glue between the standard delivery and shipping label modules.

name: delivery_carrier_manual_price
summary: Lets you type the shipping cost by hand on a sales order for shipping methods flagged Manual Price, instead of the computed rate. The flag is set on the shipping method.

name: delivery_carrier_manual_price
summary: Lets you type the shipping cost by hand on a sales order for shipping methods flagged Manual Price, instead of the computed rate. The flag is set on the shipping method.

name: delivery_carrier_manual_weight
summary: Lets you type the weight and shipping weight by hand on a transfer, for shipping methods flagged Manual Weights, instead of the computed weight. The fields appear on the transfer form.

name: delivery_carrier_manual_weight
summary: Lets you type the weight and shipping weight by hand on a transfer, for shipping methods flagged Manual Weights, instead of the computed weight. The fields appear on the transfer form.

name: delivery_carrier_max_quantity
summary: Sets a maximum quantity on a shipping method. When a sales order reaches that quantity, the carrier can no longer be selected for it. Set the Max Quantity on the shipping method.

name: delivery_carrier_max_weight_constraint
summary: Stops the package type wizard from creating a package heavier than the package type's maximum weight, when the rule is switched on. The rule can be set for the company, per shipping method or per package type, under Settings > Inventory > Shipping.

name: delivery_carrier_max_weight_constraint
summary: Stops the package type wizard from creating a package heavier than the package type's maximum weight, when the rule is switched on. The rule can be set for the company or per package type, under Settings > Inventory > Shipping.

name: delivery_carrier_multi_zip
summary: Lets one shipping method cover several zip code ranges instead of one. Set Zip Option to Ranges on the shipping method, then add a line for each zip interval. Found under Inventory > Configuration > Delivery.

name: delivery_carrier_multi_zip
summary: Lets one shipping method cover several zip code ranges instead of one. Set Zip Option to Ranges on the shipping method, then add a line for each zip interval. Found under Inventory > Configuration > Delivery.

name: delivery_carrier_option
summary: Technical base for carrier options, which are extra services that can differ from one transfer to the next and can be mandatory or applied by default. It has no visible effect on its own; carrier-specific modules build on it.

name: delivery_carrier_package_measure_required
summary: Lets you mark which package measurements (length, width, height, weight) are required on a package type, so the Put in Pack wizard cannot skip them. Transfer validation also checks that the required measurements are filled in. Needs the package dimension module.

name: delivery_carrier_partner
summary: Adds a Transporter field on shipping methods that links to a partner, so you can record which transport company runs each method. The field sits on the shipping method form.

name: delivery_carrier_partner
summary: Adds a Transporter field on shipping methods that links to a partner, so you can record which transport company runs each method. The field sits on the shipping method form.

name: delivery_carrier_picking_valid
summary: Technical helper that checks a transfer against a shipping method's requirements, such as size and volume limits. It adds validation methods and no new screens of its own.

name: delivery_carrier_picking_valid_dangerous_goods
summary: Checks a transfer or sales order against a shipping method's dangerous goods limits, so a carrier with an ADR limit is not offered for orders with hazardous products over that limit. Set the ADR Limited Amount on the Availability tab of the shipping method.

name: delivery_carrier_pricelist
summary: Calculates a shipping charge from the product price list of the shipping method, so the cost can differ by customer, date and pricelist. It adds a Based on Product Pricelist provider, and a Pricelist Cost invoice policy that overrides an external carrier's cost.
keywords: shipping cost based on price list

name: delivery_carrier_report_to_printer
summary: Lets a shipping method use a Label report that can be set to print straight to a chosen printer. A placeholder report is supplied, and the real label has to come from each carrier's integration. Set the Label report on the shipping method form.

name: delivery_carrier_shipping_label
summary: Technical module that stores shipping labels as their own attachment type on a transfer, so labels can be told apart from other documents and sent to the right printer. Carrier-specific modules use it when they create labels.

name: delivery_carrier_shipping_policy
summary: Sets a shipping policy on each shipping method, and the sales order picks it up by default. The policy is shown on the shipping method form and carried onto the sales order.

name: delivery_carrier_warehouse
summary: Lets you set a delivery method on each warehouse. When a customer has no default carrier, the Add shipping wizard uses the warehouse's method. Set on the warehouse form under Inventory.

name: delivery_carrier_warehouse
summary: Lets you set a delivery method on each warehouse. When a customer has no default carrier, the Add shipping wizard uses the warehouse's method. Set on the warehouse form under Inventory.

name: delivery_cbl
summary: Connects shipping methods to the CBL courier web service. Shipments are registered when an outgoing delivery is validated, labels are generated, shipments can be cancelled, and a CBL manifest can be produced. The provider takes CBL credentials plus freight type and cash on delivery options.

name: delivery_correos_express
summary: Connects shipping methods to the Correos Express API. When a delivery is confirmed the shipment is recorded at Correos Express, and the shipping reference and labels are logged in the chatter. Set up as a delivery method with Correos Express as the provider.

name: delivery_cttexpress
